passages.text:
INTERNSHIP MANUAL Description The University's recognition of the importance of providing practical learning experiences through the Student Internship Program in the Philippines (SIPP) reflects its commitment to holistic education.
It understands that classroom instruction alone may not fully prepare students for the challenges and complexities they will encounter in the professional world.
As such, the University embraces the idea that real-world exposure is indispensable to their growth and development.
By adhering to the Commission on Higher Education's (CHED) CMO No. 104 s. 2017, which outlines revised guidelines for SIPP across all programs, the University demonstrates its dedication to keeping its internship program up-to-date and relevant.
These guidelines serve as a framework that ensures the internship experiences are structured, meaningful, and aligned with the learning objectives of each academic program.
Through the internship program, students gain a deeper understanding of the practical applications of their theoretical knowledge.
They are provided with opportunities to immerse themselves in actual work environments, where they can witness firsthand how various industries operate, how professionals tackle real challenges, and how teamwork plays a crucial role in achieving success.
Beyond simply observing, students are encouraged to actively participate in the tasks and projects assigned to them during their internships.
This hands-on experience not only strengthens their technical skills but also fosters their ability to adapt and innovate.
They are encouraged to propose creative solutions to problems, which allows them to think critically and apply their academic learning in a practical context.

passages.title: UC-PnC Internship Manual
passages.source: University LMS / UC-PnC Internship Manual
passages.text:
Furthermore, the internship program nurtures students' communication and interpersonal skills.
They interact with professionals, clients, and colleagues, learning how to articulate their ideas effectively and work harmoniously within a team.
These soft skills are invaluable in any career and contribute significantly to their professional growth and success.
The University's commitment to the internship program underscores its dedication to producing well-rounded graduates who are not only academically competent but also equipped with practical experience and relevant skills.
The goal is to empower students to be confident and capable as they embark on their careers after graduation.
In conclusion, the University's Student Internship Program serves as a vital bridge between classroom learning and real-world application.
It enriches students' academic journey, prepares them for the challenges of the professional world, and ultimately shapes them into competent, skilled, and confident individuals ready to make meaningful contributions to their chosen fields.
Relevant to Internship Coordinators and Student Interns Responsible Officer Director, Placement, Alumni, and Linkages Department All College Deans Year Approved 2023 Dissemination The guidelines articulated in this manual are uploaded and viewable through Quality Document Management System (QDMS).

MESSAGE FROM THE CITY MAYOR/ CHAIRMAN OF THE BOARD Binabati ko kayo ng pinakamainit at taos-pusong pagbati habang inyong sinisimulan ang mapagpabagong paglalakbay ng propesyonal na paglago at pag-unlad sa pamamagitan ng programa ng internship.
Ang karanasang internship ay naglilingkod bilang isang mahalagang tulay sa pagitan ng akademikong kaalaman at praktikal na aplikasyon.
Ito ay isang hakbang patungo sa isang kinabukasang puno ng mga oportunidad, at pinapupurihan namin ang bawat isa sa inyo sa pagtanggap ng mahalagang karanasang ito sa pag-aaral.
Sa aktibong pakikilahok sa mga internship, inyong itinatag ang pundasyon para sa isang matagumpay na karera at inyong hinuhubog ang lakas-paggawa ng kinabukasan ng ating lungsod.
Sa paglalim ninyo sa inyong mga tungkulin, hinihimok namin kayong lubos na gamitin ang oportunidad na ito.
Lubos na magpakalugod sa inyong trabaho, nang buong puso'y umalam ng kaalaman, at aktibong makilahok sa mga organisasyon na nagbukas ng kanilang mga pintuan upang kayo'y tanggapin.
Ang praktikal na mga kakayahan, kritikal na pag-iisip, at propesyonal na mga network na inyong maipapaunlad sa panahong ito ay magiging mahalagang yaman sa buong inyong mga karera.
Naniniwala kami sa inyong potensyal at sa malaking kontribusyon na inyong magagawa sa inyong mga larangan.
Tandaan na ang lungsod ay nakatindig nang malakas sa likod ninyo, nagbibigay ng suporta, mga kagamitan, at isang network ng mga oportunidad upang tiyakin ang inyong tagumpay.
HON.
DENNIS FELIPE C.
HAIN (Sgd) City Mayor/Chairman of the Board

MESSAGE FROM THE UNIVERSITY PRESIDENT Internships provide a unique opportunity for students to bridge the gap between theory and practice, allowing them to apply their knowledge in real-world settings.
The hands-on experience gained through internships not only equips our students with the necessary skills but also cultivates a deeper understanding of their chosen fields.
It is through these experiences that they develop the resilience, adaptability, and critical thinking abilities that will serve them well in their future endeavors.
To our student interns, I encourage you to approach your internships with enthusiasm and a willingness to learn.
Take advantage of every opportunity to engage with your colleagues, seek guidance from your supervisors, and immerse yourself fully in the tasks and projects assigned to you.
To our internship coordinators, I extend my heartfelt gratitude for your unwavering support and guidance.
Your commitment to cultivating meaningful relationships with our industry partners, identifying valuable internship placements, and providing ongoing mentorship is truly commendable.
Your dedication ensures that our students receive the best possible opportunities to develop their skills and expand their professional networks.
As we move forward, I encourage all of you to embrace the values of integrity, professionalism, and collaboration throughout the internship process.
Treat each other with respect, foster an inclusive environment, and prioritize open communication.
Together, we can create an atmosphere where learning flourishes, and the impact of internships is maximized.
Wishing you all a successful and enriching internship experience.
DR.
CHARLEMAGNE G.
LAVIÑA (Sgd) University President III

MESSAGE FROM THE VICE PRESIDENT FOR ACADEMIC AFFAIRS An internship can be an important first step in your career as it provides valuable hands-on work experience to complement your academic studies.
This internship manual serves as a comprehensive resource to support your success throughout your practicum journey.
It is important to familiarize yourself with the goals, objectives, and expectations of both the University of Cabuyao and the partner school, organization, or firm where you will be interning.
By understanding the guidelines outlined in this manual, you can effectively coordinate your training plan and maximize the learning opportunities presented during your on-the-job training experience.
The manual also provides information on the organization's communication practices, which should serve as a guide for your professional growth.
Additionally, keeping a weekly progress report will help ensure you stay on track to achieve your objectives, and these reports will be reviewed by the respective faculty practicum coordinator.
Remember to adhere to deadlines and requirements and maintain regular contact with your faculty practicum coordinator to demonstrate your commitment and appreciation for the organization where you are interning and to uphold the honor of the Dangal ng Bayan.
Your reports will contribute to the continuous improvement of the University of Cabuyao's on-the-job training program and guidelines.
By making meaningful connections and demonstrating professionalism, you can build a positive reputation during your internship.
We wish you the best of luck and hope you thoroughly enjoy your internship experience.
DR.
RENELINA D.
MAÑABO (Sgd) Vice President, Academic Affairs

MESSAGE FROM THE VICE PRESIDENT FOR STUDENT DEVELOPMENT AND AUXILIARY SERVICES Welcome to the internship program of the University of Cabuyao (Pamantasan ng Cabuyao)!
We are delighted to present you with the University's Internship Manual, designed to provide you with valuable guidance and support as you embark on your internship journey.
This manual serves as a comprehensive resource to help you navigate the exciting and rewarding world of internships, equipping you with the necessary tools to make the most of this crucial phase in your academic and professional development.
Internships play a pivotal role in bridging the gap between theory and practice, offering you the opportunity to apply your classroom knowledge to real-world scenarios.
They allow you to gain practical experience, develop essential skills, expand your professional network, and explore potential career paths.
By engaging in internships, you will not only enhance your resume but also lay a strong foundation for your future endeavors.
Remember, your internship experience is what you make of it.
Embrace the opportunities, be proactive, and maintain a positive and professional attitude throughout.
Your dedication, commitment, and willingness to learn will undoubtedly leave a lasting impression on your supervisors and colleagues.
We encourage you to utilize this manual as a companion throughout your internship journey.
We are confident that it will serve as a valuable resource, equipping you with the knowledge and skills necessary to succeed in your internship and beyond.
Wishing you a fulfilling and transformative internship experience!
DR.
FLORANTE A.
MAGNAYE (Sgd) Vice President, Student Development and Auxiliary Services

GUIDELINES
MANAGEMENT OF INTERNSHIP AT UNIVERSITY OF CABUYAO (PAMANTASAN NG CABUYAO) PNC:AA-GU-13 The University recognizes the importance of providing students with practical learning experiences through the Student Internship Program in the Philippines (SIPP).
This is in line with the Commission on Higher Education's (CHED) CMO No. 104 s. 2017, which provides revised guidelines for SIPP for all programs.
The University acknowledges that student learning should not be limited to classroom instruction alone.
Instead, students should be given the opportunity to apply what they have learned in real-world settings, where actual problems and challenges arise, and where solutions are experimented on.
Through the internship program, the University aims to provide students with this kind of exposure to further prepare them for their future careers.
The internship program is an essential component of the University's academic curriculum.
It is designed to enable students to gain practical experience and acquire essential skills that are relevant to their chosen field of work.
Through the program, students are given the opportunity to observe and participate in real work situations, to develop their problem-solving and critical thinking skills, and to hone their communication and teamwork abilities.

Section 1.
General Policies 1.
In accordance with CMO No. 104 s. 2017, the University expands its degree academic programs to meet the needs of the industry.
It fosters mutually beneficial industry-academic collaboration and linkages, as well as strengthens career guidance.
2.
The Pamantasan ng Cabuyao Internship Program is a graduation requirement that is designed to immerse students in an appropriate work environment.
3.
It will increase productivity, gain knowledge, and teach the value of respect in the workplace.
4.
PNC commits to adhering to the requirements of CHED Memorandum Order (CMO) No.4, series of 2020 and the Guidelines on the Required Health Standards in Basic Education Offices and Schools per DepEd Order No. 014, series of 2020 for the Education programs to promote the well-being of students and ensure the quality of their learning and exposure while undergoing Internship.
5.
The number of hours required from a student intern varies according to the approved curriculum of the degree program.

MESSAGE FROM THE CITY MAYOR/ CHAIRMAN OF THE BOARD Sa ngalan ng lungsod at ng pinahahalagahang Board of Regents ng Unibersidad, kami ay taos-pusong bumabati at nagpapaabot ng mainit na pagtanggap sa inyo sa University of Cabuyao.
Sa inyong paglalakbay sa larangan ng mas mataas na edukasyon, kami ay nagagalak na kayo ay maging mahalagang ambag sa aming aktibong akademikong komunidad.
Maniwala kami na ang edukasyon ang pundasyon ng pag-unlad at susi sa pagbubukas ng inyong potensyal.
Sa pamamagitan ng inyong dedikasyon, sipag, at uhaw sa kaalaman, magkakasama nating hinuhubog ang isang mas magandang kinabukasan para sa ating lungsod at sa mas malawak na pamayanan.
Ang Student Manual, na hawak ninyo ngayon, ay isang mahalagang sanggunian na idinisenyo upang gabayan kayo sa inyong panahon ng pag-aaral, nagbibigay ng mahalagang impormasyon at mapagkukunan upang malampasan ang iba't ibang oportunidad at hamon na naghihintay sa inyo.
Hinihikayat namin kayong gamitin nang lubusan ang inyong panahon sa UC (PnC).
Isanib ninyo ang inyong sarili sa kayamanan ng mga karanasan sa pag-aaral, tanggapin ang iba't ibang perspektiba ng inyong mga kapwa mag-aaral, at makisangkot sa mga pinahahalagahang mga propesor na mag-aakay at magbibigay-inspirasyon sa inyo sa buong paglalakbay.
Tandaan, ang edukasyon ay hindi limitado sa loob ng silid-aralan.
Ito ay isang paglalakbay ng personal na pag-unlad, pagtuklas ng sarili, at pagbubuo ng makabuluhang ugnayan na magpapaanyo sa inyong pagkatao at magpapalawak ng inyong kaalaman.
Nawa'y maging makulay ang inyong paglalakbay sa larangan ng pag-aaral, puno ng kasiyahan sa mga natuklasan, makabuluhang mga kaugnayan, at mga tagumpay na magpapabanaag ng kahalagahan ng inyong kinabukasan.
HON.
DENNIS FELIPE C.
HAIN (Sgd) City Mayor/Chairman of the Board

passages.page_or_section: OUR HISTORY (p. 13)
passages.text:
OUR HISTORY
On April 16, 2003, then-municipal mayor Proceso D.
Aguillo signed Municipal Ordinance No. 2003-059, "Ordinance Establishing the Pamantasan ng Cabuyao (University of Cabuyao) and Other Purposes," creating the Pamantasan ng Cabuyao (PnC).
The institution began offering classes in business administration, information technology, education, nursing, and midwifery in June 2003.
Before the Pamantasan ng Cabuyao was founded, the Laguna State Polytechnic University (LSPU) had a satellite campus at the Cabuyao National High School.
A memorandum of understanding between the mayor of Cabuyao Municipality and the LSPU president served as the basis for the LSPU's operations.
The LSPC-Cabuyao Campus began its operation in 1993 and ended on March 31, 2003.
In the latter half of 2002, faculty and students at LSPC protested against the LSPC president's leadership.
With the support of the majority of students, who were mostly Cabuyeños, the protest was found by the Sangguniang Bayan of Cabuyao to be true and based on facts.
It caused the memorandum of agreement to be terminated, and the only option left to the mayor's administration was to establish Cabuyao Community College.

passages.title: UC-PnC Student Handbook Manual
passages.source: University LMS / UC-PnC Student Handbook Manual
passages.page_or_section: OUR HISTORY (pp. 14-15)
passages.text:
OUR HISTORY
In light of the anticipated closure of LSPC-Cabuyao, faculty members under the leadership of Charlemagne Lavina and Frank Parao aided the mayor's office and advised them that the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM) is the model school for local colleges.
Dr.
Benjamin Tayabas, who was president of PLM at the time, helped the town of Cabuyao and personally oversaw the establishment of the institution.
He recommended calling it Pamantasan ng Cabuyao.
Municipal Ordinance No. 2003-059 was enacted by the Sanguniang Bayan on April 15, 2003.
The following day, Mayor Proceso D.
Aguillo gave his approval to the same.
Pamantasan ng Cabuyao was personally inaugurated by no less than President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo on June 19, 2003 on the occasion of the 107th birthday of Dr.
Jose Rizal and officially started its operations on July 31, 2003, the birthday of its founding mayor.
In 2017, the university received its Commission on Higher Education (CHED) Institutional Recognition, becoming one of the few local colleges and universities (LCUs) to receive such recognition.
The university was awarded by the Duterte Administration the right to avail of the FREE COLLEGE EDUCATION or the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary
Education (UNIFAST) under the Republic Act 10931 – becoming one of the 76 LCUs in the country to be given such right to free education in 2019.
To date, PnC has been awarded by ALCUCOA with twelve (12) Level 2 and two (2) Level 1 programs.
The higher level of accreditation is a testament to the university's commitment to providing free quality education, especially to its talented marginalized student populace.
Today, PnC is one of the few leading local colleges and universities in the Philippines with level 2 accredited programs.

The university produced topnotchers in the fields of education, nursing, and engineering.
Forward-looking, PnC envisions itself becoming the premier leading local university in Region IV by further elevating its academic standards, thereby producing value-laden and globally competent graduates and continuously striving for improvement in quality services in instruction, research, and extension.
PnC commits itself to the holistic education of every "Dangal ng Bayan", thereby producing graduates that bring pride and honor to the nation.

passages.text:
UNIVERSITY SYMBOLS
THE UNIVERSITY LOGO The logo features a green circular outer layer.
It symbolizes the university's commitment to environmental sustainability and community development by representing the Cabuyao land.
The six-pointed stars within the layer represent the University's founders, implying that the University was founded by a group of six people who shared a common vision and goal for the school.
The inner layer of the logo depicts Cabuyao's legendary Kampanang Ginto.
A shield-shaped design with a white-gray background is contained within the bell.
The shield is blue to represent the sky, which represents the pursuit of knowledge and wisdom.
This also emphasizes the University's commitment to produce graduates that bring pride and honor to the nation.
Within the shield is the year 2003, the year of the University's establishment.
The image of the Cabuyao Municipal Hall below represents the university's close relationship with the local government and commitment to serving the community.
On top of the Cabuyao City Hall is an engineering triangle that represents
strength, stability, and balance.
It also symbolizes the university's dedication to providing a solid foundation for engineering education.
The caduceus is a well-known ancient symbol associated with medicine and healthcare.
It also symbolizes the university's strong focus on health-related programs.
The stylized flame in the middle of the shield represents the spirit of innovation and creativity.
The flame also represents the university's commitment to promoting entrepreneurship and inspiring its students to be leaders in their respective fields.
Under it is an open book, which represents the pursuit of knowledge and the importance of education in the university's mission.

UNIVERSITY SYMBOLS
The atoms are written in an open book and convey the university's emphasis on science, research, and the pursuit of knowledge.
The gear on top represents the university's commitment to providing education in engineering, technology, and innovation.
The gavel represents authority, order, and leadership and its intention to offer preparatory programs for law academic program.
The lighting represents the university's dedication to fostering creativity, inspiration, and new ideas.
The quill pen is associated with the University's arts and sciences program.
A dove holding an olive branch represents the element of peace.
These symbols represent the university's dedication to fostering peaceful coexistence and understanding among various cultures and communities.
Below the image is the university's mantra, "Peace, Prosperity, and Service," which conveys the university's commitment to fostering economic growth and development on a local and global scale, as well as the university's ethos of giving back to society and making a positive difference in the lives of others.

passages.text:
UNIVERSITY SYMBOLS
UNIVERSITY MACE The University of Cabuyao mace is a regally designed symbol of academic authority and prestige that embodies the rich heritage and traditions of the university.
With its prominent university emblem displayed atop a polished wood staff adorned with intricate carvings, the mace serves as a visual reminder of the institution's commitment to providing quality education, fostering intellectual growth, and shaping the future of its students.
Displayed during ceremonial occasions, the mace inspires a sense of pride and unity among the university community, reinforcing the collective commitment to academic excellence and the pursuit of knowledge.
UNIVERSITY MEDALLION The University of Cabuyao medallion worn by the University President is a symbol of esteemed leadership and authority.
The medallion showcases the university's emblem or crest at the forefront.
Crafted from high-quality materials, the medallion exudes a sense of prestige and significance.
As a distinguished accessory worn by the University President, it represents the highest level of academic and administrative responsibility.
It is a visual embodiment of the university's values, traditions, and commitment to excellence, symbolizing the leader's role in guiding and shaping the institution's future.

INSTITUTIONAL QUALITY POLICY Pamantasan ng Cabuyao commits to adhering to statutory and regulatory requirements, promoting high levels of customer engagement, and maintaining an effective quality management system through periodic review and communication of quality objectives for continuous improvement of quality services in instruction, research, and extension.

To promote analytical thinking among the faculty and students for continuing intellectual growth and advancement of learning and research.

To develop the youth to become responsible leaders, as well as productive and actively involve citizens of the local and global community with good values and excellent character.
3.
To preserve, enrich, and transmit the historical, cultural heritage, and desirable Filipino values and character.
4.
To nurture an integrated multi-disciplinary university that promotes excellence in instruction, research, and extension.

To be the research and development arm of the local government unit.

The University of Cabuyao has established clear and transparent admission and enrollment guidelines to ensure a fair and efficient process for prospective students.
To be admitted into the university, applicants must meet the specified academic requirements, which may vary depending on the desired program of study.
T Once admitted, students proceed with the enrollment process, where they officially register for their chosen courses and programs.
It is essential for students to carefully follow the provided guidelines and deadlines to secure their place and successfully enroll in the University of Cabuyao.
By implementing these admission and enrollment guidelines, the University of Cabuyao aims to maintain a systematic and organized process that ensures a seamless transition for students from application to enrollment, ultimately allowing them to embark on their academic journey at the university.

CHAPTER I STUDENT ADMISSION PNC:SDAS-GU-12 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
Pamantasan ng Cabuyao shall admit students of good moral character, those who comply with the required school credentials, and those who are willing to abide with the University established guidelines.

CHAPTER II STUDENT ENROLMENT PNC:AA-GU-19 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
A student who qualifies for enrollment is eligible to stay for the entire period in which s/he is expected to complete the program in the University, without prejudice to his/her right to transfer to other schools and without violating the University's rules and regulations.
2.
A student may enroll after the lapse of the regular enrollment period specified in the approved school calendar and be admitted in accordance with reasonable rules of the University for late enrollment, but in no case shall exceed two weeks after the opening of classes.
Thereafter, no further enrollment shall be allowed.
3.
A student is deemed officially enrolled after submission of appropriate initial requirements; has made the initial payment of school fees for non-free Higher Education beneficiary and other fees to the University; and allowed to attend classes by the University.
A notarized Affidavit of Undertaking (PNC:AA-FO-35) shall be submitted by the student prior to enrollment.
Admission or transfer credentials shall be submitted within the semester.
Otherwise, enrollment in the succeeding term will not be permitted.
4.
For purposes of enrollment, the name and other personal data or circumstances of each student as indicated in the PSA Certificate of Live Birth or Alien Certificate of Registration, where applicable, shall prevail.
5.
No foreign students shall be allowed to enroll without the appropriate requirements from the educational institution, Commission on Higher Education, and Bureau of Immigration.

Enrollment Schedule.
Schedule of semestral enrollments which are reflected in the Academic Calendar shall be posted on the website, social media platform, and strategic places in the University and barangay offices at least a month prior to its conduct.
Likewise, the final course offerings prepared by the Department Chair, endorsed by the Dean, and verified by the Registrar shall be posted and uploaded in PnC Facebook Page and iMPnC a month prior to enrollment.
2.
Enrollment Requirements for Old Students. a.
Students under the following conditions shall not be given access to their enrollment accounts unless they settle their deficiencies and accountabilities or given considerations by the concerned department head. i.
With back accounts at the Cashier; ii.
With accountabilities or deficiencies in the other offices; iii.
With pending disciplinary case; iv.
Failed 25% and above of the total number of units required in their particular program. b.
Blocking and unblocking of students' enrollment account is done through the system.
3.
Year Level.
A student shall be considered in a particular year level if s/he has already earned the number of units required in the preceding level.
The year level status shall be used in determining the courses to be offered by the system to the student enrollees.

Student Load.
The approved curriculum for each program dictates the student's study load and course sequence.
In certain circumstances, exceptions may be granted based on the student's best interest and educational system objectives a.
A regular load is the required number of units in a semester/ term as per the curriculum based on the student's academic year or classification. b.
During the Mid-year, a regular load is 9 units.
However, graduating students may be allowed to take a maximum load of 12 units. c.
Simultaneous courses in a pre-requisite and advanced courses may be permitted for students who are graduating at the end of the school year under the following conditions: i.
If the pre-requisite is a repeated subject; or ii.
If the student has a good academic standing. d.
In some cases, the Registrar may approve an overload of six units to a student of any year level, considering their academic performance in previous semesters and the total course load once the additional six units are added.

i.
A student may only be granted an overload once during their entire time at the university.
The six-unit overload, which cannot exceed 30 units, cannot be split into semesters.
Overloaded courses must be in the same semester, and prerequisites and corequisites must be strictly followed. ii.
To make any adjustments to a student's load, the Request for Student Load Adjustment (PNC:AA-FO-43) must be completed and processed.
The Department Chair should recommend it, and the Dean should endorse it before the Registrar approves it.
The Registrar's staff will automatically update the system with any changes. iii.
Only students without failing grades, dropped courses, or incomplete remarks are eligible for an overload.
6.
Shifting of Curricular Program a.
When grades are available, students intending to shift to another program must complete an application form (PNC:AA-FO-44), either offline or online.
Admission of the shifter depends on the evaluation and approval of the Dean of the accepting department unit.
Once approved, the sending department must be notified. b.
The Dean must inform students of the potential graduation delay that may result from shifting programs. c.
The basis in crediting courses are: i.
Course title and course description.
The course to be credited must have the same course title or, as the required course in a desired program. ii.
Number of units.
The number of units of the credited course must be equal to or greater than the units required in the desired program.

Shifting from one program to another is allowed however the students shall be disqualified for UNIFAST.
Students are only allowed for two times during the duration of the students' entIre stay in the University.
7.
Off-semester courses.
The Dean may offer off-semester courses to assist the irregular students to graduate on time.
Cost shall be shouldered by the students.
Offering of off-semester courses could be through petitioned. a.
Petitioned Classes are offered as requested by the students through filling out of Petitioned Class Form available at the Office of the University Registrar. b.
The requesting students should meet the class size requirement of 15 students.
Otherwise, total cost shall be divided among the interested students. c.
PNC:AA-FO-52 Application for Petitioned Class Form shall be processed to facilitate the request. d.
Students cannot withdraw their application once the petitioned class has been approved.
Otherwise, the Cashier's Office shall include the assessment cost to their student ledger and shall be paid within the semester.
8.
Withdrawing from the Roll. a.
Course/s officially dropped within the first two weeks and within the first four days of classes during regular and midyear, respectively, shall be entitled to a refund and shall not be reflected in the student's permanent records and in the enrollment reports of the University.
The Dropping of Courses and Withdrawal Form (PNC:AA-FO-45) shall be used for this purpose. b.

9.
Dropping from the Roll. a.
During regular semester, students who will drop a course within six weeks from the first day of classes will be considered officially dropped.
The Dropping of Courses and Withdrawal Form (PNC:AA-FO-45) shall be used for this purpose. b.
Students who incurred absences of more than 20% of the total number of school days except for valid reasons shall be given a mark of 5.00 for Graduate School and College and 74% for SHS. c.
If majority of the excessive absences incurred is excused, the student should be given a grade of "UD" with the remark "EEA" or "excessive excused absences." However, if the majority of the absences incurred are unexcused, he should be given a grade of 5.0 with the remark "excessive unexcused absences" or "EUA." 10.
Enrollment in courses with overlapping schedules shall not be allowed.
11.
Cross Enrollment. a.
From Pamantasan ng Cabuyao to Other HEIs. i.
With the written consent of the University and for valid reasons, a student may be allowed to cross enroll in another recognized higher educational institution for courses that are not typically offered during a specific term. ii.
Cross-enrollment is usually permitted only if:
• The desired course/s are not offered in the University during the student's current enrollment term
• The course is available, but its schedule conflicts with the student's other classes.

Professional courses should be taken within the University, and the total load, including cross-enrollment courses, should not exceed the regular load within the semester. iv.
During a given semester, a student can only cross-enroll in one school. v.
The student is responsible for paying the corresponding enrollment fees at the other higher educational institution. vi.
The Application for Cross-Enrollment (PNC:AA-FO-46) must be completed and processed to facilitate cross-enrollment.
It must be approved by the Dean, Registrar, and Vice President for Academic Affairs. vii.

To cross-enroll in academic or non-academic courses from another institution, a student must obtain a written permit from the Registrar of their home institution.
This permit should indicate the total number of units and specific courses that the student is required to take at PNC. ii.
Upon obtaining the written permit, the student must complete the Application for Cross Enrollment (PNC:AA-FO-46) and pay the corresponding enrollment fee at the Cashier's Office.

13.
Leave of Absence a.
The Leave of Absence (LOA) refers to the absence of a student from the university.
During LOA, the student is not enrolled in any course, not considered a bonafide student, or not allowed to enter the campus, except as a visitor to transact with certain offices. b.
The student must submit the Request for Leave of Absence (PNC:AA-FO-48) on or before the last day of late enrollment if they plan to go on LOA.
The LOA period should not exceed one year, but an extension can be requested by accomplishing the same form. c.
Undergraduate students are expected to enroll continuously until they complete their program.
If they need to interrupt their studies, they must file for an approved LOA, which implies that they will be accepted as a returnee subject to university policies. d.
Students on LOA are not allowed to enroll or study in other educational institutions, and no course taken by them from other schools can be credited toward the completion of their program in this university. e.
If a student withdraws from the college without an approved LOA, their registration privileges will be limited or completely withdrawn.
14.
Once the concerned authorities have signed an application submitted to the Office of the University Registrar, it will be considered as final and valid.
However, the submission of the application form does not guarantee approval.
Therefore, it is essential for the student to follow up on the status of the application three (3) working days after submission.

PART 2. ACADEMIC GUIDELINES
The University of Cabuyao has established clear and comprehensive academic policies to ensure the smooth and fair administration of student-related matters.
These policies cover various areas, including student examinations, issuance of academic records, transfer of credits in collegiate programs, semestral academic honors, grading systems for senior high school, college, and graduate school, management of educational trips and off-campus activities for both college and senior high school students, as well as senior high school and college graduation requirements.
These guidelines are designed to uphold academic integrity, maintain consistent standards, and support the overall educational experience and success of students at the University of Cabuyao.

CHAPTER I STUDENT EXAMINATION PNC:AA-GU-11 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
Uploading and administration of tests are facilitated thru the iMPnC (PinnaCle).
Teaching personnel may opt to administer the examination onsite or thru other external learning tool such as Google Form and MS Form, among others.
2.
Examinations must be reviewed by the Department Chair two weeks before the scheduled examination before uploading to Pinnacle or administering in other forms.
3.
The weight of examination in the grading system is as follows: a.
College (For lecture, it is 50% of the grading system and for laboratory it is 60% of the grading system). b.
Graduate School (It is 40% of the grading system) c.
Senior High School (Quarterly assessment is 25% for core subjects, 30% for academic track, and 20% for Technical-Vocational and Livelihood.
Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
Senior High School a.
Quarterly examinations are given in all subjects. b.
Examinations are validated by the Principal or SHS Coordinator. c.
Type of Examinations.
The type of examinations is usually situational analysis and application which bring out critical thinking and related skills among the learners. d.
Post-Test Evaluation.
Learners are allowed to countercheck the answers in the examination thru the LMS or other platforms adapted by the Senior High School.
e.
Grading System.
It adopts a based zero grading system.
2.
College a.
The examination schedules are announced by the Office of the University Registrar and the Dean's Office before the start of classes. b.
Examinations in college are scheduled by the Registrar and Academic Head for six days based on the actual class schedule so as not to have conflicts. c.

The Deans shall observe departmental examination. d.
Other evaluative measures such as cultural presentation, immersion, recitation, or quizzes shall be reflected in the e-class record (igrade.pnc.edu.ph) with corresponding weight or percentage to complete the final grade.
Quizzes must be explicitly written on the class record and shall always be part of the grade.
Project not included in the Outcomes-Based Teaching and Learning Plan (OBTLP) is not allowed. e.
Teaching personnel who opt to give exemption during the final examinations must explain ahead (e.g. during the orientation meeting/first class meeting) the mechanics of exemption.
This must be part of the OBTLP. f.
Written complaints on test checking can be entertained before the final recording on the class record. g.
Missed Examinations.
A student who misses a major examination automatically obtains a raw score of zero unless his/her failure to take the test is excused. h.
Special Examinations.
Special examination may be given to a student who missed a major examination upon presentation of the approved application form (PNC:AA-FO-32). i.
The examination must be taken not later than seven
calendar days after the original schedule of examination.
The schedule shall be defined by the Office of the University Registrar. ii.
Valid reasons accepted are sickness and death of immediate family member.
Students who have qualified in academic and non-academic competitions may be requested by the Department Chair/Coordinator to take the examination until the encoding of grades. i.
Missed Quizzes.
A student who misses a quiz due to unexcused absence will automatically obtain a raw score of zero. j.
Mock Board Examinations.

In order to prepare for the board/licensure examinations, graduating students in BS Accountancy, Nursing, Psychology, Education, and Engineering are expected to take mock board exams.
Results of the mock board exams are provided to the students within a week or according to a set schedule, and students who do not pass are offered intervention programs by the respective department.
The collegiate departments follow a zero-grading system, whereby a final grade of at least 60% is required to pass the course and receive credit for the unit/s.
3.
Reviewing, Returning, and Discussing Test Papers a.
All examination papers are automatically returned to students online via PinnaCle, providing valuable feedback on their class performance.
If done through other platforms, test papers must be returned by the teaching personnel. b.
Students must be given the opportunity to clarify their corrected exams and receive their grades. c.
During their consultation schedule, teaching personnel should discuss the corrected examination with students so that they are aware of their areas for improvement in the relevant course.

PART 2. ACADEMIC GUIDELINES > CHAPTER II ISSUANCE OF STUDENTS ACADEMIC RECORDS > Section 1. General Policies
CHAPTER II ISSUANCE OF STUDENTS ACADEMIC RECORDS PNC:AA-GU-20 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
Every student is entitled to receive copies of their academic records and other credentials from the University, provided that the student has settled all financial obligations and property responsibilities with the school.
2.
The University has a responsibility to furnish students with copies of their academic records and other credentials, as long as the student does not have any outstanding financial obligations or property responsibilities with the school.
3.
In cases where a student is under penalty of suspension or expulsion, the release of their school or academic records and other credentials will be at the discretion of the school, either at the end of the penalty period for suspension or with approval from the Department of Education or Commission on Higher Education for expulsion.
4.
The right to access and receive one's school records is an individual right granted to the student by law.
However, in the case of a minor, this right may be exercised by their parents or legal guardians.
5.
Except under lawful court order or when necessary for public safety or order, school records cannot be disclosed to any other individual.
To allow for data processing, sharing, and disclosure in compliance with the Data Privacy Act of 2021, students must provide a signed Academic Credential Authorization Form (PNC:AA-FO-51).
6.
The Office of the University Registrar is responsible for managing and processing personal and sensitive personal data of students
for various purposes, such as sharing academic and scholastic records with parents/guardians, academic institutions, government agencies, and private or public corporations.

Students are required to sign a Data Privacy Consent during enrollment to authorize these actions.

8.
Under the provisions of the Data Privacy Act of 2021, students have the right to request the correction of personal and privileged information.
To initiate such a request, students must submit the PNC:AA-FO-53 Request for Correction of Student's Personal Data to the Office of the University Registrar, attaching relevant documents such as a PSA/NSO Birth Certificate or Marriage Contract.
Failure to provide the necessary documentation will render the form null and void.

The student is required to obtain the Request for School Records (PNC:AA-FO-56) form from the Office of the University Registrar and complete it. b.
To ensure the validity of the request, the requesting or claiming party must present two (2) valid identification cards with their signatures during the processing of the request. c.
The Registrar's staff will provide a Payment Slip, which the student must present to the Cashier for payment. d.
The student is responsible for paying the required fee for the requested academic credential at the Cashier's Office. e.
After making the payment, the student must present the Official Receipt back at the Office of the University Registrar. f.
A Claim Slip will be issued to the student. g.
The student will need to wait for the requested documents to be prepared and issued. h.

If a student or graduate is unable to personally claim their requested school or academic record, they must complete the Academic Credentials Authorization Form (PNC:AA-FO-51).
3.
Issuance of Diploma and TOR of Graduates a.
The issuance of the Diploma and Transcript of Records (TOR) will be observed upon the completion of all graduation
requirements outlined in the PNC:AA-GU-24 Senior High School, Collegiate, and Graduate School Graduation document.
Both documents will bear the Special Order Number issued by DePEd or CHEDRO-IVA, respectively.

Degree programs that have achieved "accredited status" from an accrediting agency and are recognized by CHEDRO-IVA are exempted from requiring special order numbers (as per CMO 1 s. 2005). b.
The diploma will be presented to graduates during the graduation ceremonies, except in cases where the special order number from CHED has not yet been released. c.
The fees for the Diploma and TOR for graduates are included in the graduation fee. d.
The original diploma is issued only once.
However, the University accepts requests for a "second copy" of the diploma, subject to the following conditions: i. that the words "Second copy issued on (date)" are printed on the second copy of the diploma; ii. that in case the signatories of the original diploma are no longer in the University, the school officials who have replaced them shall sign on the succeeding copies. e.
The school officials shall issue and/or award TOR to graduates during the graduation ceremonies provided: i. they are cleared from all financial and/or property responsibility with the University; and ii. they have submitted their Terminal Clearance on scheduled date. f.
Requests for additional copies of the Transcript of Records (TOR) are permitted, without any limitations on the frequency or number of copies requested.
The purpose for which the request is made (e.g., board exam, evaluation, employment, further studies) must be specified, and the series number of issuance will be indicated on the TOR.

4.
Issuance of TOR to Student who will Transfer Out a.
The TOR of transferees must be released to requesting student only upon acceptance of the official request which is included in the Certificate of Eligibility to Transfer.
This is an indication that the transferring student has already submitted the required document to the requesting school to which s/he is transferring. b.
All TOR, whether released to the student or sent to the requesting schools, must be sealed with the signature of the Registrar signed on the flap of the envelope. c.
Requests made by a school for TOR which is already released to another school cannot be honored.
The second school must request the TOR from the school to which the transcript was first released. d.
A Certificate of Transfer Credential (PNC:AA-FO-56) signed by the University Registrar shall be issued not later than two weeks after the filing of the application for transfer, provided that, in the case of a student who is a transferee from another school, his/her records from that previous school that have been received are complete, and in order. e.
TOR shall be released provided that financial/property obligations have been settled by the requesting student.
5.
Issuance of TOR for other purposes a.
The University may issue a Transcript of Records (TOR) to students, whether they are alumni, undergraduates, or transferring out of the institution, provided that the purpose of the request is clearly stated in the document.
This includes purposes such as employment, study abroad, board/licensure exams, visa/passport applications, application for correction of name to DepEd, or for evaluation purposes.

6.
Issuance of other school or academic records a.
The Office of the University Registrar will provide various credentials for scholarship, evaluation, employment, CAV (Certificate of Authentication and Verification), transfer, and similar purposes.
These credentials may include certification of grades, enrollment, earned units, medium of instruction, and other relevant information. b.
The Certificate of Eligibility to Transfer will be issued only once.
A second copy may be requested in cases where the original copy has been lost or damaged, and an affidavit of loss is presented as supporting documentation. c.
If a student who has been issued a Certificate of Eligibility to Transfer decides not to proceed with their transfer to another school, they must return the documents to the Office of the University Registrar for cancellation, provided that the certificate has not been used for enrollment in other schools.
The acceptance of the student by the University will be subject to management approval. d.
Requested credentials will be processed and released within the same day or a maximum of seven working days, depending on the workload of requests. e.
All unclaimed requests for school or academic records will be disposed of after a period of 90 calendar days.
7.
TOR Request for Students who Transferred to the University a.
Request for SF10/TOR of students who transferred to the University shall be processed during the 1st quarter for SHS and within their first semester of attendance for college.
PNC:AA-FO-57 Request for SF10/Transcript of Records shall be prepared by the Office of the University Registrar. b.

Authentication of school or academic records a.
Students and/or graduates may apply for authentication of school or academic records issued by the Office of the University Registrar. b.

11.
Confidentiality and Security of Records a.
Compliance with the rule on confidentiality of student records would be applicable only in the case of "classified or strictly "confidential records" of the student and does not necessarily apply to "unclassified or non-confidential" records. b.
Some of these classified records or documents are, but not limited to, the following: i.
Personal and academic records of the student; ii.
Baptismal or birth certificates; iii.
Adoption papers; iv.
Academic reports; and v.
Disciplinary records. c.
Confidential records should be released only upon the request of: i. the student owning the records; ii. the parents or guardian, if the student is a minor; iii. the other school officials and/or teachers in the school system who have legitimate educational interests; iv. the officials of other school in which the student seeks to enroll; v. the authorized representatives of government including state educational authorities, as long as records are not identifiable to a particular student; vi. organizations conducting studies for, or on behalf of, educational agencies if the personal identification of the student is destroyed when it is no longer needed for the study; and vii. accrediting organizations. d.
Moreover, the records must be released i. upon a valid court order.
However, a court order may be refused by invoking the question of privilege (like that of the priest and confessant) and requesting a ruling from the highest court of justice;
ii. or in connection with a student's application for or receipt of financial aid; and iii. as warranted by regulations of government entities pertaining to health or welfare of student or other persons. e.

Its integrity shall be regularly assessed by the personnel at the Office of the University Registrar, in coordination with the Management Information Systems Department.
12.
Withholding of Credentials a.
The transfer credential of a student may be withheld by the Pamantasan ng Cabuyao due to reasons such as suspension, expulsion, non-payment of financial obligations, or failure to fulfill property responsibilities. b.
The release of the credential will be granted promptly upon settling the outstanding obligations or upon completion of the suspension or expulsion penalty. c.
Transfer credentials will not be issued to students during the semester in which they are currently enrolled.

CHAPTER III RETENTION GUIDELINE FOR ALL ACADEMIC PROGRAMS PNC:AA-GU-10 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
The program requires that students must adhere to the retention guideline upon admission.
2.
The retention guideline of the University applies to the first, second, and third-year students of the different colleges and Senior High School, providing a suitable and effective provision.
3.
The guideline aims to provide suitable and effective interventions to encourage students to meet the requirements of their respective fields.
Its purpose is to filter out students who are not meeting the minimum course requirements, and for board programs, to increase the likelihood of graduates passing board exams.
Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
Classification of Students for Board and Non-Board Programs a.
With Good Standing.
Any student who receives passing grades or higher in all courses enrolled for the semester shall be classified as good standing. b.
Warning.
A student who did not pass 25% of his/her courses enrolled in one given semester shall be warned by the Dean and Department Chair using the prescribed form (PNC:AA-FO-18) to improve his/her work.
The student shall be asked to write the promissory letter expressing intent to improve his/ her grade/s or risk being put on probation.
The letter shall
be signed by the parents/legal guardian.
Two consecutive warnings will lead the students to probation status.
Three (3) succeeding warnings will lead the students to dismissal. c.
Probation.
A student who did not pass more than 50% of his/ her courses enrolled in one given semester shall be put on probation.

A consultation with the student and parent shall be facilitated by the Program Chair and Dean.
An Academic Contract (PNC:AA-FO-19) shall be signed by all parties concerned.
His/her load shall be reduced by three units.
A probationary students who receives a warning on the following semester will be dismissed from the university.
Students who receive an Inc grade will be assigned a Probationary status unless they complete their studies before the enrollment period.
Academic Competency Examination for Students (ACES) shall be given to those who have completed their first and second year curriculum.
Student who will fail the said examination shall be given Probationary Status.
A consultation with the student and parent shall be facilitated by the Department Chair and Dean.
An Academic Contract (PNC:AA-FO-19) shall be signed by all parties concerned. d.
Dismissal.
A student who did not pass 75% of his/her courses enrolled in one given semester shall be dismissed immediately.
Students shall be permanently barred from readmission to any programs of the University.
Parents/Guardian shall be informed of the status of the concerned student.
2.
The rule on dismissal does not apply to the following: a.
Students whose grades of 5.0 were incurred due to incorrect encoding of the teacher; and b.
Senior students or students in the last curriculum year of their curricular program.

3.
The following retention policy shall be observed for Graduate School students. a.
A student who accumulates a total of nine units of failure in any course subject is automatically dropped from the program. b.
A student who receives a failing grade in any component of capstone project/thesis writing may re-enroll during the next term.
The student should not exceed the residency period (i.e. 5 years) in the program. c.
Students who stop enrolling unofficially in a semester in any Graduate School degree program shall be asked to enroll in refresher courses as follows: No. of unattended semester No. of units (refresher course) One (1) year 3 units Two (2) years 6 units Three (3) years 9 units More than three years Back to zero 4.
The Maximum Residence Rule (MRR) states that students who fail to finish the requirement of any degree program within a prescribed period of actual residence shall not be allowed to register further in the program.
Under meritorious cases, extension of residency may be granted.
Each extension granted shall be recorded through the University Registrar.
5.
The prescribed years to finish a degree program are as follows: Degree Program Maximum years of residency Four-year Baccalaureate Degree Program Six (6) years Master's Degree Program Five (5) years 6.
The following retention policy shall be observed for Senior High School students (DepEd Order No. 13 s. 2018 and DepEd Order No. 8 s. 2015
a.
A student who incurred a final grade of at least 75% in all learning areas in a semester shall proceed to the next semester. b.

CHAPTER IV SEMESTRAL ACADEMIC HONORS/ACHIEVERS PNC:AA-GU-22 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
The Office of the University Registrar will publicize the list of students who have achieved Semestral Academic Honors or recognition through various means such as the University website, social media platforms, and notices posted in key locations on campus.
The announcement will be made within five days after the completion of the semester.
2.
The following Academic Honors/Awardees shall be given every semester to qualified students: a.
President's List refers to college student with at least 1.25 semestral grade point average and with no grade lower than 92% in any course. b.
Vice President for Academic Affairs' List refers to college student with semestral grade point average from 1.26 to 1.50 and with no grade lower than 88% in any course. c.
Dean's List refers to college student with semestral grade point average from 1.51 to 1.75 and with no grade lower than 80% in any course. d.
With Highest Honors refers to SHS student with semestral weighted average from 98 to 100% and no grade lower than 85% in any subject shall qualify. e.
With High Honors refers to SHS student with semestral weighted average from 95 to 97% and no grade lower than 85% in any subject shall qualify.

passages.text:

f.
With Honors refers to SHS student with semestral weighted average from 90 to 94% and no grade lower than 85% in any subject shall qualify.
Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
To be eligible for Semestral Academic Honors (SAH), students must be enrolled in the full semestral load as required by their curriculum.
2.
Students who have advanced courses but are still enrolled in the full load can still qualify for SAH.
3.
Students who wish to be considered for academic honors must not have repeated any course in any educational institution and must not have incurred any grade lower than a "satisfactory" (Inc), "dropped" (Drp), or failed (Fail) remark or rating in the semester they are being evaluated for SAH.
4.
Students who have been found guilty of major disciplinary action after due process are not eligible for SAH.
5.
To recognize students who excel academically in their program of study, certificates will be awarded to all SAH awardees/honorees during the Recognition Rites scheduled by the Office of the University Registrar.
The Recognition Rites may be held online or onsite.
6.
The University will provide financial incentives to students who rank in the top 10 per program every semester with a general weighted average (GWA) of 1.5 or higher, and no grade lower than 1.75.
7.
The rule of rounding off numbers to the nearest hundredths must be strictly followed.

passages.text:
PART 2. ACADEMIC GUIDELINES > CHAPTER V SENIOR HIGH SCHOOL, COLLEGIATE, AND GRADUATE SCHOOL GRADING SYSTEM > Section 1. General Policies
CHAPTER V SENIOR HIGH SCHOOL, COLLEGIATE, AND GRADUATE SCHOOL GRADING SYSTEM PNC:AA-GU-24 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
The Office of the University Registrar has specified a date for students to view/download their computerized card, and it is the responsibility of the teaching personnel to encode their students' grades in a timely manner.
2.
Within ten days after the last day of examination for the first and second semesters, and within five days for the midyear, encoding of students' grades must be completed.
3.

It may be given due to extenuating circumstances, such as illness or family emergencies, that prevent the student from completing the required work on time ii.

Graduating students who received an incomplete grade/s in their last semester and failed to complete on or before the deliberation shall not be part of the graduation rites.
However, the student shall be allowed to complete the grades within the next semester.
S/he shall join the next commencement exercises.
Failure to complete the grades within the next semester shall result in obtaining a grade of 5.0, consequently re-enrolling the course. v.

Request for Change of Grades.
The request for a change of grade is a serious matter that affects not only the students but also the credibility of the institution.
Thus, the following guidelines must be observed and complied with:
• Grades duly signed and submitted are considered final and permanent.
However, if the teaching personnel requests a grade change, the only valid reason for such a request is when it is the teacher's fault.
Any other reasons will not be accepted.
Likewise, a student questioning his/her grade is insufficient grounds for changing the grade.
• The request for a grade change must undergo a thorough evaluation and is subject to the President's final approval.
• The teaching personnel requesting the change of grade must also submit a notarized affidavit and admission/ declaration of his/her error.
This affidavit will prove the teacher's accountability for the error.

Senior High School Grading System a.
The K to 12 Basic Education Program uses a standard- and competency-based grading system.
All grades will be based on the weighted raw score of the learner's summative assessments. b.
A final grade of 75% is necessary for the subject to be considered passed and/or for the units to be credited.
The lowest grade that can appear on the report card is 60 for quarterly and final grades. c.
The sum for each component is converted to the Percentage Score (PS).
To compute the Percentage Score (PS), divide the
raw score by the highest possible score then multiply the quotient by 100%.

CHAPTER VI MANAGEMENT OF EDUCATIONAL TRIPS, AND OTHER OFF-CAMPUS ACTIVITIES OF COLLEGE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS PNC:AA-GU-14 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
Educational tour refer to curricular off-campus learning activities involving mobility of students with the supervision of authorized personnel outside the premises of the institution which lasts for more than one (1) day, and involves relatively more places of destination than a field trip in accordance with specific degree program requirements (CMO 63 s. 2017).
This covers visits to reputable firms or government sites; culture and arts-related activities such as visits to museums, cultural sites, landmarks, and other related venues; and plant industry visit, host training establishment visits, and other related visits.
2.
Field trip refer to curricular off-campus learning activities involving mobility of students with the supervision of authorized personnel outside the premises of the institution but is of relatively shorter duration usually lasting for only one (1) day, and with fewer places of destination (CMO 63 s.2017).
3.
According to CHED Memorandum Order No. 63, s. 2017, as well as CHED Memorandum Order 26, s. 2015, and subsequent memoranda in 2018, the University is required to abide by the policies and guidelines for local off-campus activities and international trips for undergraduate and graduate students.
4.
The University is responsible for designing, determining, and approving off-campus activities that align with the curriculum requirements and the University's philosophy and objectives.

The Entrepreneurial and Business Development Department, through an Accredited Service Provider, must coordinate in advance and properly with local government units, including obtaining a letter of acknowledgement from the concerned government agency before any scheduled educational tours, field trips, or related off-campus activities.

Additionally, transportation vehicles to be used must be deemed roadworthy.

Approval in writing from the University is required before conducting any curricular or non-curricular off-campus activities.

These activities must be aligned with the program or course and be included in the OBTLP with a specified weight.
However, they cannot be used as a substitute for major exams to compel students to participate in non-compulsory educational activities.
10.

11.

12.

Students joining educational tours and/or field trips shall secure a medical clearance from the school clinic duly signed by its physician or authorized representative prior to the date of educational tour, field trip, and related off-campus activities.

8.
Academic requirement a.
Approval of proposed educational activity i.
Duly accomplished Request for Local Off-Campus Activity accompanied by a detailed plan must be submitted by the faculty concerned to the Academic Dean for discussion and validation at most one month after the receipt of the faculty workload.
The plan shall include the following:

It is the duty of faculty-in-charge or the faculty handling the course to determine whether the student qualifies to join the educational tour, field trip, or related off-campus activities.
For International tour, the following requirements shall be observed:

• Faculty handling the course;

• Others who may be requested by the academic head. vii.

As such, the concerned faculty must have prior knowledge on the destination. viii.

CHAPTER VII USE OF PINNACLE, THE LEARNING MANAGEMENT SYSTEM OF THE UNIVERSITY PNC:AA-GU-12 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
The Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, in coordination with the Management Information Systems Department, is responsible for the administration of the PinnaCle.
2.
They are responsible for the management and administration of all aspects of the LMS including but not limited to: a.
User-interface components and design, navigation links, and tool configuration and availability b.
Course components including site design and structure, course codes, and term designations.
Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
User Management and Access a.
All bonafide teaching personnel and students shall be given access rights in the PinnaCle. b.
All users shall be authenticated with unique credentials and use the PinnaCle for official purposes only. c.
All users of the LMS are responsible for maintaining the security of usernames and passwords.
Access credentials may not be shared or given to anyone other than the user to whom they were assigned. d.
To ensure privacy, protection of intellectual property and the integrity of materials, access to courses in the PinnaCle is regulated. e.
Delivery and access to learning resources in LMS must adhere to guidelines set forth in the University's Intellectual Property policy.

All teaching personnel are responsible for their own course content, assignments, and any other related materials.

passages.text:
PART 2. ACADEMIC GUIDELINES > CHAPTER VIII SENIOR HIGH SCHOOL, COLLEGIATE, AND GRADUATE SCHOOL GRADUATION > Section 1. General Policies
CHAPTER VIII SENIOR HIGH SCHOOL, COLLEGIATE, AND GRADUATE SCHOOL GRADUATION PNC:AA-GU-23 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
Upon the completion of all academic and other requirements for graduation, a student will be recommended for graduation.
Candidates for graduation are listed as of the end of that semester if they completed all requirements by the set deadline.
2.
A student cannot be considered graduate from the University unless they have completed at least 50% of the residence work required, although this may be extended under certain circumstances.
Additionally, the student must have settled all property and monetary obligations.
3.
Graduation date is set and reflected in the school calendar, usually held a month after the final examinations in the SHS and collegiate departments.
4.
The Office of the University Registrar facilitates the deliberation of candidates for graduation and academic honors during the Academic Council meeting.
5.
The Graduation Committee, led by the Vice President for Academic Affairs and co-chaired by the University Registrar, carefully plans and executes graduation ceremonies.
6.
The Dean and Registrar recommend a graduating student to the CHEDRO IVA for issuance of Special Order Number after completing all academic requirements and settling financial/ property obligations with the University.
7.
The official list of graduates is submitted to DepEd and CHEDRO-IVA immediately after graduation.

Residency Requirement: Students must finish their program of study within the prescribed residency period as stated in PNC:AA-GU-11.
Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
The Office of the University Registrar allows college students to apply for graduation every first semester of the academic year at the University.
This is done by filing an application for graduation (PNC:AA-FO-60) at the Office of the University Registrar.
2.
Graduation Requirements.
Only students who have completed the following requirements shall be recommended for graduation and shall be allowed to graduate and/or participate in the graduation ceremonies and be printed in the graduation program and yearbook. a.
For College i.
Passed all courses in their respective curriculum program ii.
Accomplished the Curricular Program Evaluation (PNC:AA-FO-62) and terminal clearance (PNC:AA-FO-61); and iii.
Applied formally for graduation (PNC:AA-FO-60). b.
For SHS i.
Passed all subjects; and ii.
Accomplished the terminal clearance.
3.
Candidates for Graduation a.
The tentative list of candidates for graduation shall be generated after the preliminary examination for the college/ graduate school and after the third quarter examination for the Senior High School. b.
The official list of candidates for graduation shall be posted two days after the deadline for submission of the terminal
clearance in strategic places in the University and thru website and official PNC social media accounts. c.

All candidates for graduation shall be applied for Special Order from the CHED Regional Office at least sixty calendar days before the end of the semester for the tertiary level.
Degree programs which have attained "accredited status" by an accrediting agency and recognized and as per advised by CHED ROIV are exempted from special order numbers (CMO 1 s. 2005). i.
Students with inconsistent name or spelling must be corrected first before recommending for Special Order. ii.
The University shall use the Special Order format required by CHED. iii.
Recommendation for Special Order must be:
• per graduate and must bear the date of graduation;
• signed by the Registrar and attested by the Dean;
• by program and must have a maximum of 10 graduates per certification;
• notarized. iv.
The Office shall immediately attend to disapproved request for Special Order. v.
A month after the release of student's grades, the Registrar shall request for cancellation of Special Order of candidates who have failed to satisfy the academic requirements of their respective programs.
4.
Deliberation of Candidates for Graduation Honors and Awards a.
The Academic Council shall convene within one month after the last day of the final examination for graduating students to deliberate on the candidates for graduation honors.
Only graduating students with complete academic records at the time of the deliberation shall be qualified for honors.
The
candidates and their academic records shall be presented by the University Registrar. b.
Deliberation results shall be immediately posted on the bulletin boards of the Office of the University Registrar. c.

passages.text:
PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS
Welcome to the Student Success section of the Student Manual.
At Pamantasan ng Cabuyao, we are committed to providing you with an enriching educational experience that extends beyond the classroom.
We believe that your success as a student is not solely measured by grades, but by your holistic growth, personal development, and achievement of your goals.
This section of the manual aims to equip you with valuable insights, strategies, and resources that will empower you to thrive academically, socially, and personally during your time at PnC.
We understand that each student's journey is unique, and we are here to support you every step of the way.
Student success is about more than just completing coursework and earning a degree.
It encompasses your ability to navigate the challenges and opportunities that arise, build meaningful connections with peers and mentors, and cultivate essential skills that will serve you well in your future endeavors.
Remember, your success as a student is a partnership between you and the institution.
It requires dedication, resilience, and a proactive approach to your education.
By taking advantage of the opportunities available to you and embracing a growth mindset, you will not only excel academically but also develop into a well-rounded individual prepared for the challenges and triumphs that lie ahead.
We are excited to embark on this journey with you and celebrate your achievements along the way.
Together, let us create a vibrant and supportive community where student success is not just a goal, but a reality for each and every one of you.

CHAPTER I ACADEMIC CONSULTATION AND CLASS/YEAR LEVEL ADVISING PNC:AA-GU-09 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
The teaching personnel is responsible for creating a schedule for academic consultation and class/year level advising, if applicable.
The involved parties are then informed of the schedule.
2.
The Dean/Principal recommends class/year level advisers to the VPAA for review and approval at least one week prior to the start of the semester.
Once approved, the VPAA will issue an appointment paper to the concerned advisers.
3.
If a teaching personnel is unable to address identified behavior/ attitude problems of a student, the SASD Director can be referred to in coordination with the Guidance and Counseling Department.
This is done using the referral slip.
4.
The department is expected to collaborate with other units/ departments/offices in addressing identified learning weaknesses and improving student performance.
5.
A summary of academic consultation/level advising should be used to create an action program/activities.
6.
Class/Year Level Advisers work closely with the Dean/Principal, Program Chair, and Student Affairs and Services Department to provide high-quality co-curricular services to students of Pamantasan ng Cabuyao.
Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
The Faculty Teaching Load requires all teaching personnel and Class/Year Level Advisers to include their weekly schedule of
academic consultation and indicate the location or platform for such activity.
2.
The schedule and venue/platform of academic consultation and Class/Year Level Advising must be readily available to the Academic Head, students, student council, and various student organizations.

CHAPTER II SPORTS DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM AND SERVICES PNC:SDAS-GU-01 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
All health protocols, rules, and regulations regarding the return of sports in the new normal set by the local and national agencies must be followed.
2.
All facilities, leagues, or tournaments shall be monitored by the Director for Sports and Development Department, in coordination with the Coaches.
3.
The University shall participate in sports competitions organized by Association of Local College and Universities Athletics Association (ALCU-AA) and Department of Education, among others.
Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
On recruitment. a.
The primary objective of Pamantasan ng Cabuyao's recruitment program is to maintain academic standards while maintaining the competitive strength of varsity players to maximize the funding provided by the City Government for the organization's sports development program. b.
Following are the eligibility/qualifications: i.
Bona fide students of the University; ii.
Enrolled in at least 12 units of course load in the current year; iii.
With passing weighted average with no failure; iv.
Has no record of any case of misconduct in school; v.
Age Eligibility (25 and under for Collegiate Athletes, 18 and under for High School Athletes); and
vi.
With PNC-UC Medical Clearance and PNC-UC Psychological clearance c.
Potential student athletes shall submit the duly accomplished Application Form (PNC:SDAS-FO-01) to the Director for Sports and Development Department d.
Recruitment shall be managed by the Director for Sports and Development Department.
An evaluation form (PNC:SDAS-FO-02) shall be utilized in assessing applicants. e.

This period is divided into general and special preparatory stage.
There are two and a half to three months in the general preparatory stage, which is always longer than the second stage.
It guarantees quantitative work; when the player's capacity for training load changes, a higher amount of training is always feasible.
One of the key aspects of how the work is organized at this point is the increased training time given to general preparation in all training areas.
In
this stage of training, practically all results of motor abilities increase. ii.
The special preparatory stage last approximately one to two months.
It ensures the players' form through a qualitative training.
As a primary element influencing the training load, training intensity gradually replaces training volume.
The focus of all training gradually increases while group and team activities receive increasing time.
Only a few unique motor skills are further developed; general motor skills remain at their current level. c.
Competitive Period/Season (3 to 4 months).
The major goal of this exercise is to maintain the players' physical condition at all times.
The main emphasis of the training is on the outcomes of games and other activities. d.
Post Competitive Period/Off-Season (1 month).
The major objectives of this period are to eliminate the tiredness accumulated over the training year and refill the depleted energy stores.
Most athletes are subjected to a variety of psychological and social stressors over the months of training and competition, which depletes their mental energies.

7.
Discipline System for Members of PNC-UC Athletes a.
Demerits System i.
To instill discipline and correspondingly to attain training objectives, a demerit system shall be imposed wherein trainees start each month with zero demerit.
Depending on the type of offense or infraction, demerits are given, and those who exceed at the end of each month the maximum allowable number of (60) demerits shall be subjected to disciplinary action. ii.
While it is primarily left to the discretion of the official coaches, some of the guidelines for prescribing demerits are:
• Unauthorized absence - 10 demerits
• Failure to comply with the days training exercises - 5 demerits
• Willful disobedience - 2 demerits
• Misbehavior during Training (quarrelling, making fun of others) - 2 demerits
• Unauthorized departure from training area - 2 demerits
• Stealing - 10 demerits iii.
Disciplinary Action.
Players who accumulated (60) demerits for any two consecutive months or those found physically/mentally unfit shall be suspended or dropped from the team as determined by the Director, Sports and Development Department upon recommendation of the coaches.
8.
Moral Values Rules and Regulations a.
Trainees shall abide all moral values imposed by the Director, Sports and Development Department.
Details are as follows: i.
No public display of affection between opposite sex at all
occasions and places with the bounds of all PNC-UC sports activities, be it training or event proper. ii.
No coach-athlete mutual relationship. iii.
Disciplinary Action
• First offense: one-year dismembership from the program.
