Smoking, drinking alcoholic beverages, stimulants drugs and gambling inside and outside the quarter are prohibited. ii.
Change of assigned room without prior knowledge of the coaches/PNC-UC sports officials and quarrelling of others are valid ground to suspend or remove the athlete from the team. iii.
PNC-UC varsity players are not allowed to enter or sleep in any quarters. iv.
Disciplinary Action
• First offense: one-year dismembership from the program.
• Second offense: automatic termination from the program.
9.
Physical Fitness Conditioning and Handling of Injuries and Illness a.
All athletes–varsity training pool and reserved players – are required to undergo physical conditioning exercises. b.
All athletes are required to perform their exercise routines regularly.
Those who fail to perform their exercise routines regularly without justifiable reason may be removed from the varsity program. c.
Any injury directly related to sport participation that occurred during team travel, supervised practice, and supervised strength and conditioning sessions shall be handled by the coaches, in coordination with the Director for Sports and Development Department.

d.
The concerned students shall be endorsed by the Coach to the University Health Department.
First aid shall be given immediately. e.
For serious cases, the parents/legal guardians or persons identified by the varsity-athlete to be contacted during emergencies shall be notified by the University Health Department. f.
If necessary, the varsity-athlete shall be transferred to a hospital of choice or nearest government hospital by the University Health Department. g.
A petty cash amounting to Php 5,000 shall be issued to the SDD Director during emergency cases.
It shall be liquidated within two days upon receipt. h.
All medical abstracts and necessary report shall be submitted to the SDD Director for insurance processing at the Accounting Office. i.
The University Health Department shall prepare an Incident Report and submit the same to the VPSDAS. j.
The Sports and Development Department does not and cannot cover any personal illnesses (chronic or acute - at any time), any infection, diagnostic tests or surgery for preexisting conditions, or injuries incurred by a student-athlete outside of team travel, scheduled contests, supervised practice and supervised strength and conditioning sessions.
This includes injuries incurred prior to enrolling at the University, recreational or intramural sports participation and any personal fitness activity. k.
Under no circumstances, the coaches shall not allow injured athletes or those coming off illness to resume training or participate in competitions without a certification from the University Health Department that the athlete is physically fit to resume his/her athletic activities.

10.
Varsity Athletes Exemption in Physical Education Classes a.
A student-athlete enrolled in PE courses shall be recommended for exemption by the Director for Student and Development Department to the faculty concerned. b.
Such arrangement shall take effect only after a thorough screening of the Director for Student and Development Department and approval of the Vice President for Student Development and Auxiliary Services and Vice President for Academic Affairs. c.
The coaches shall submit the grades of the Varsity Player to the concerned teaching personnel through the Director for Sports and Development Department.
11.
Athlete of the Year Award a.
The University shall give award and recognition to outstanding athletes and to those who have shown exemplary contribution to their chosen sport and have given prestige to the University. b.
The award shall be given to the athlete during the Recognition Day. c.
The criteria for each award include: i.
Has played during the last year in the University ii.
Played for the University for at least six consecutive semesters iii.
Has demonstrated leadership and cooperation with team members iv.
Has demonstrated sportsmanship in every game v.
Has an average scholastic record of 77% to 80% vi.
Has no derogatory record.
12.
Coaches a.
The recruitment, selection, and hiring of coaches shall be facilitated by the Human Resource Management Department.

b.
Coaches shall facilitate preparation of the Daily Time Record, which shall be endorsed by the SDD Director to the HRMD. c.
In order to avoid conflicts of interest, hired coaches must not train athletes from competing schools. d.
Coaches shall be evaluated by the varsity team (PNC:SDAS-FO-06) and the SDD Director (PNC:SDAS-FO-07) at least one month before the contract expires. e.

CHAPTER III RECOGNITION AND RENEWAL OF STUDENT ORGANIZATIONS PNC:SDAS-GU-08 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
The establishment and operation of student organizations in all colleges and universities are governed by the then Department of Education, Culture and Sports Department Order No. 61 s. 1985 which provides rules and regulations concerning student organizations and their activities within the school campus.
2.
Students who want to form a student organization should follow the regulations promulgated by the University through the Student Affairs and Services Department (SASD).
3.
The University reserves the right not to admit organizations espousing goals/activities contrary to the philosophy and objectives of the institution.
4.
All recognized student organizations, college student government, and student councils are directly under the jurisdiction and supervision of the SASD.
5.
All guidelines governing the recognized student organizations, college student government, and student councils shall be made by the SASD.
6.
Membership fees may be collected among students as indicated in the Constitution and By-Laws and as needed.
This shall be coordinated with the SASD Director.
Management of fund shall be monitored by the Adviser and the SASD Director.

passages.text:
PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER III RECOGNITION AND RENEWAL OF STUDENT ORGANIZATIONS > Section 2. Specific Policies
Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
Application for Recognition a.
Recognition of student organizations is made official once they are given the certificate of recognition.
Official recognition shall be effective for one academic year or one semester only under special circumstances. b.
The following organizations should seek approval for recognition from SASD: i. newly-formed organizations; ii. organizations which became inactive for at least one semester; and iii. probationary organizations, which include suspended organizations that have been existing for two years. c.
Any group of at least 20 members intending to form a student organization may apply to SASD. d.
The following documents must be prepared at the time of application: i.
Accomplished application form to be issued by the SASD (PNC:SDAS-FO-15); ii.
Proposed Constitution and by-laws; iii.
Student Leader's Profile with 1 x 1 recent photo (PNC:SDAS-FO-16); iv.
Adviser's Profile with 1 x 1 recent photo (PNC:SDAS-FO-17); v.
List of Active Members (PNC:SDAS-FO-18); vi.
Adviser's Agreement Form (PNC:SDAS-FO-19) vii.
Annual Project Plan (PNC:SDAS-FO-20) e.
The SASD shall deliberate on the merit of the applicant organization based on the documents submitted.
The applicant organization shall be informed of the results of the deliberation (approved or disapproved) five days after the submission of the requirements.
PNC:SDAS-FO-15 Page 2 shall be used by the SASD Director in evaluating the applicant student organization.

f.
The recommended list of recognized student organizations, college student government, and student councils shall be endorsed to Vice President for Student Affairs and Auxiliary Services for approval.
Once approved, the Certificate of Recognition shall be given during the recognition ceremony.
2.
Renewal of Recognition a.
Recognized student organizations and student councils applying for renewal of recognition should submit the following to SASD: i.
Renewal Form (PNC:SDAS-FO-15); ii.
Student Leader's Profile with 1 x 1 recent photo (PNC:SDAS-FO-16); iii.
Adviser's Profile with 1 x 1 recent photo (PNC:SDAS-FO-17); iv.

Annual Project Plan (PNC:SDAS-FO-20) vii.
Notarized Constitution and By-Laws viii.
After-Activity Report (PNC:PRE-FO-26); and ix.
Activity Financial Statement (PNC:SDAS-FO-21). b.
The renewal of recognition/accreditation of student organization is a precondition for its operation in the University.
A Certificate of Recognition shall be given to the organization's full compliance with the requirements. c.
Non-compliance with the requirements and procedures of the evaluation process also means automatic disqualification of the student organizations concerned. d.
Student organizations who failed to meet the criteria for evaluation set by the SASD shall be dropped from the roster.
They are allowed to re-apply for recognition after a year of reprieve observing the procedures for Application for Recognition. e.

3.
Recognition Status.
Student organizations which qualify for recognition may do the following: a.
Use of university facilities, equipment, and services, following the provisions on the use of such; b.
Conduct any activity in the name of the University; c.
Participation in university-wide activities and if necessary, city-wide activities, or LGU-sponsored ventures; d.
Inclusion of the organization's name in various publications of PnC-UC; e.
Inclusion in the annual search for Outstanding Student Organization (OSO) Award and Outstanding Student Leader (OSL) Award f.
Represent the school in any seminar / conference outside the University. g.
Conduct fund raising activities in coordination with the SASD and Office of the Vice President for Student Development and Auxiliary Services h.
Attend the yearly Lilukan, the Leadership Training Program 4.
Non-Recognition of Student Organizations a.
Student organizations and student councils shall not be recognized on the basis of the following reasons: i.
The student organization habitually violates SASD policies on student organizations and student activities. ii.
The student organization has been given severe penalty as a result of the said violations b.
After the annual evaluation of student organizations, the SASD Director shall notify the student organizations through written communication who failed to qualify for recognition. c.
All appeals for reconsideration of the decision made by the SASD shall be addressed to the Vice President for Student Affairs and Auxiliary Services
5.
Rehabilitation of Non-Recognition of Student Organizations a.

SASD shall help non-recognized student organizations who intend to regain their official recognition.
The program is not a guarantee for eventual recognition of the student organization concerned.
It is only a means to provide learning experience for organizations who want to improve themselves. b.
Student organizations who wish to undergo the rehabilitation program should signify their intention to do so in writing addressed to the SASD Director. c.
SASD will conduct a conference with the said organization to discuss further their concerns. d.
Based on the results of the said conference, the SASD shall design a developmental program suited for the requesting organization. e.
The SASD shall enlist the help of other recognized student organizations to be its partners in implementing the program. f.
Student Functions and Assemblies i.
Student functions and assemblies can be conducted and/or participated in by securing the approval of the authorities concerned.
All proposals of the activities should be submitted to SASD one (1) month before the scheduled date of activity (PNC:SDAS-FO-20). ii.
Five days after the conduct of the activity, student organizations shall submit an Activity Financial Statement (PNC:SDAS-FO-21) (if applicable) and After-Activity Report (PNC:PRE-FO-26) with documentary pictures of the activity duly signed by the Adviser.
Official receipts must also be attached. iii.
All financial reports shall be checked by the SASD Director.

6.
Selection of RSO, CSG, SC, and USG Adviser a.
The recognized student organizations, college student government, and student councils shall select their adviser according to the qualifications set forth by SASD. b.
Any full-time non-teaching and teaching personnel may perform advising role to the student organizations as long as he/she meets the qualifications set forth by SASD. c.
Each student organization selects an adviser subject to the approval of the SASD Director. d.
Student organizations must have only one adviser.
An adviser should only have one student organization to be monitored every academic year. e.
The following are the qualification standards for advisers: i.
S/he is a full-time teaching or non-teaching personnel in the University. ii.
For academic-related organizations, an adviser must have an academic preparation, professional training, or experience related to the organization s/he is advising. iii.
For non-academic student organizations, the adviser must be knowledgeable of the organization's area of specialization. iv.
S/he has at least a "Very Good" evaluation rating based on previous advisees' evaluation (PNC:SDAS-FO-22) v.
S/he has a good moral character, with personal integrity and has not been subjected to any grievance or disciplinary proceedings during the period of his /her employment in the University. vi.
S/he has strong commitment and willingness to devote time and effort to student development. vii.
S/he has good leadership and interpersonal skills and is committed in maintaining harmonious and pleasant personal and official relations with other teaching and non-teaching personnel and administrators of the University.

Attend the meetings of the organization and note pertinent issues raised by the group/ members. viii.
Attend meetings called by SASD h.
Recruitment of Members i.
Recruitment of members apply only to non-academic organizations since membership to an academic organization is based on the program where the student is enrolled. ii.
All non-academic recognized student organizations may recruit, orient, and induct new members after acquiring permission from the SASD Director. iii.
The SASD will schedule the recruitment week for non-academic organizations.
It is usually done on the first month of classes. iv.
Duly recognized organizations may recruit members only during the period prescribed by SASD for university-wide organization or college-based organizations. v.
Recruitment, selection, orientation, and/or initiation conducted by any recognized student organization shall be subjected to the following limitations:
• No recruitment, selection, and orientation shall be conducted one week prior to the scheduled major examination.
• Initiation rites involving violence, public humiliation, verbal abuse, body contact, physical pain, harassment, mental torture, or subjecting applicant to do mental torture, or subjecting applicant to do something beyond human dignity is absolutely prohibited.
• Violations of these provisions on recruitment, selection, and orientation of prospective members shall cause the automatic cancellation of the Certificate of Recognition given to the organization without prejudice to any disciplinary action and/or criminal prosecution against the organization and its members.

i.
Membership/Officership in Organization i.
All bonafide PnC-UC students may serve as a member in one non-academic student organizations aside from their respective academic organizations where membership is compulsory. ii.
Students are allowed to assume leadership positions in only one organization. iii.
All organization officers must be in good academic standing i.e., have no failing grades in the last two semesters. iv.
Members of the USG may also join in any recognized organizations in PnC-UC. j.
Evaluation of Recognized Student Organizations and Student Council i.
All RSOs, CSGs, SC, and USG shall be evaluated using the PNC:SDAS-FO-23. ii.
Evaluators are the SASD Director (60%) and the Adviser (40%). iii.
Student organization which has the highest evaluation result shall be declared as the Outstanding RSO/CSH/SC of the Year.

CHAPTER IV SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAM AND SERVICES PNC:SDAS-GU-09 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
In collaboration with the Student Scholarship and Financial Assistance Officer, the Director of Student Affairs and Services will process student applications for government-sponsored scholarships in accordance with their guidelines.
2.
All students are eligible to apply for any scholarship as long as they meet the program's eligibility requirements.
3.
No scholar is permitted to accept more than one scholarship from the university.
A student is eligible to receive or apply for additional scholarships offered by various private and public organizations.
4.
If the grantee does not adhere to the terms of the scholarship grant and/or in the event of a breach of the University's current policies stated below, the scholarship may be terminated.
This will result in forfeiture of the scholarship once the VP SDAS's decision has been authorized.
5.
Following disqualification, a student is not eligible to rejoin the same scholarship program.
However, if spots are still available for the scholarship being applied on, resigned scholars may still submit an application.
Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
Tertiary Education Subsidy (TES) for Filipino citizens a.
University Registrar shall facilitate the implementation of RA 10931 Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act of 2017. b.
For repeat courses, the student shall pay the corresponding rate per course.

2.
CHED Tulong-Dunong a.
The Student Affairs and Services Department shall manage the program.
These may be availed when students have a GWA of 2.0-2.25 and have no failing grade. b.
The Office of the University Registrar and Cashier's Office shall provide the necessary documentation.
3.
Student Assistantship Program (Source: PnC-ManCom 2022-50) a.
The total number of student assistants shall be dependent on the budget allocation given by the PnC-UC. b.
Following are the details of the scholarship. i.
Eligibility
• Only bona fide students of Pamantasan ng Cabuyao are qualified to apply.
• Residency of one-year
• No failing grade during the previous semester ii.
Requirements
• Duly accomplished PNC:SDAS-FO-24
• Class Schedule
• Copy of Grades iii.
Duties & Responsibilities
• Report to their respective office assignment at least 2 hours per day- minimum of 10 hours per week
• Submit PNC:SDAS-FO-25
• Submit a monthly Accomplishment Report duly signed by the Department Head (PNC:SDAS-FO-26)
• Daily Time Record (DTR) (PNC:SDAS-FO-27)
• Subject themselves for evaluation at the end of every Semester (PNC:SDAS-FO-28) iv.
Compensation
• Php50.00/hour 20hours per week
• May apply for overtime as recommended by the department head and approval by SASD Director
v.
Conditions
• Render work during vacant hours.
No student will be on duty when classes are held asynchronously
• Render work based on their declared duty hours and official work hours of the University
• Does not render work during exam week
• Does not render overtime hours unless requested and approved by the SASD and VP SDAS
• Does not render overtime during Saturday/Sunday
• Render office work only c.

The department head shall evaluate the student assistant before the end of the semester. d.
Student assistant who has incurred Unsatisfactory rating shall be removed from the scholarship.
4.
Sui Generis Scholarship Program. a.
It is a new program which is exclusive for Pamantasan ng Cabuyao students. b.
It aims to select qualified students in order to produce topnotchers in board examinations. c.
The scholarship shall be awarded to the top twenty (20) SGSP exam passers from each board program (Accountancy, Education, Engineering, Nursing) and additional 10 SGSP exam passers for all non-board programs. d.
SGSP examination shall be administered as scheduled in Pamantasan ng Cabuyao.
It shall cover the following course areas: i.
Mathematics ii.
Science iii.
English iv.
Specialized Courses
• STEM for those who will take engineering and health allied courses;
• ABM for those who will take Bachelor of Science in
Accountancy (BSA);
• HUMSS for those who will take Bachelor of Elementary Education (BEED) and Bachelor of Secondary Education (BSED) e.
Following are the details of the scholarship. i.
Eligibility
• Filipino citizen;
• Bona fide resident of Cabuyao;
• Only 10% of non-cabuyeneos shall be accommodated.
• Senior High School (SHS) graduates of;
• Graduating SHS students;
• Must have a General Weighted Average (GWA) of at least 85%; and
• ALS completers within the last two (2) years who are qualified to enroll in college ii.
Requirements
• Duly accomplished PNC:SDAS-FO-29
• PSA authenticated Birth Certificate;
• Barangay Certificate of Residency;
• High School Report Card for SHS Graduates;
• Certificate of Enrollment for Graduating SHS students; and

• Certificate of Completion with recommendation for ALS completers. iii.
Benefits
• free tuition and miscellaneous fees,
• Php20,000.00 per semester,
• an additional financial assistance in taking licensure examinations (for board programs). iv.
Retention
• A scholar shall have the following responsibilities:
• Enroll in a regular load per semester/term;
• Maintain a general weighted average (GWA) of at least 1.75 per semester and with NO grades below 2.50 including NSTP and PE
• Acquire no Incomplete (INC), Dropped (DRP), Unofficially Dropped (UD) or Failed grade;
• Demonstrate good moral character and exemplary conduct; and
• Complete the program within the time frame required in the curriculum; f.
Application Procedure i.
All applicants must accomplish the SGSP Application Form (PNC:AA-FO-29) which may be downloaded at www.pnc. edu.ph or may be secured from SASD ii.
Submit the accomplished SGSP Application Form together with the documentary requirements in the SASD Office on or before the specified date. iii.
The schedule of qualifying examination shall be posted through the PNC Official Facebook page or PNC website. iv.
Test permit shall be secured by the applicant from the SASD Office a week before the examination period g.
Examination Procedure i.
Examiners should bring only test permit, black ballpen, and school ID or any valid ID. ii.
Go to your designated Testing Room on the date and time specified in your Test Permit. iii.
Be in the Testing Room at least 30 minutes before the start of the examination. iv.
The test administration will last about one (1) hour and thirty (30) minutes. v.

CHAPTER V MANAGING IN-PERSON AND REMOTE STUDENT ACTIVITIES PNC:SDAS-GU-10 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
Student activities can be conducted and/or participated in by securing the approval of the authorities concerned through SASD.
2.
All proposed projects and activities shall be reflected in the Annual Project Plan (PNC:SDAS-FO-20).
Once approved, the organization shall submit individual Letter of Request (LR) (PNC:AF-FO-30) for each activity.
3.
In cases of activities which are not reflected in the project plan form, Letter of Request (LR) (PNC:AF-FO-30) shall be submitted to the same office at least 45 working days before the conduct of the proposed activity.
A letter of justification shall be submitted if the organization failed to comply with the given period of time.
4.
Submission of other pertinent requirements and observance of all SASD prescribed rules and regulations in the conduct of such functions/assemblies are vital for the approval of the proposed activity.
5.
Activities held without approval are considered illegal and may be considered a ground for administrative sanction of the proposed activity.
6.
In case the student functions/assemblies shall require the use of campus facilities online or remotely, a separate arrangement with the authorities concerned shall be made by the sponsoring organization or group as soon as the SASD has approved the activity.

7.
No student activities shall be conducted one week before the start of any major examination.
8.
Student organization shall not use the name "Pamantasan ng Cabuyao," its official logo, in any activity (i.e., fair, seminar, fieldtrip, tour, contract, announcement, etc.) or on any manufactured item unless duly authorized by the SASD.

PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER V MANAGING IN-PERSON AND REMOTE STUDENT ACTIVITIES > Section 2. Specific Policies
Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
Social Affairs a.
A social affair/concert shall be supervised by the adviser and concerned authorities.
The services of police officers/barangay officials, in addition to security guards, may be employed for the activity. b.
These events shall not go beyond 11pm and it must be ensured that security measures are strictly observed and directly supervised by the adviser and the officers of the concerned student organization.
In exigency cases, activities that will extend the allowable hour shall be approved by the VP SDAS.
2.
Fund-Raising Projects/Solicitation a.
A fund-raising activity must be motivated by an objective consistent with the philosophy and objectives of the University and the thrust of the sponsoring recognized student organization. b.
Duly recognized student organizations may be allowed to sponsor only one major fundraising activity per semester.
These shall be monitored by the SASD Director and Adviser. c.
Tickets or any related materials shall not be released without prior approval from SASD. d.
Application for fund-raising activities shall include activity objectives, ticket prizes (if applicable), beneficiary, manner as to how the funds shall be used, financial projection, and budget plan, and brief description of how the project shall be implemented. e.
In case of a raffle project, prizes must be displayed at some strategic place on campus before the raffle takes place.
If the prize is in the form of cash or small items, such should be publicly announced through posters before the raffle date.

the SASD within ten (10) working days after the activity.
Failure to do so shall be a ground for withdrawal of the recognition of the organization. g.
All monetary solicitations should be duly reviewed by SASD and VPSDAS, endorsed by the Executive Vice President and approved by the University President.
3.

Symposium, forum, etc. drawn from a desire to fulfill the University philosophy and objectives may be implemented by the concerned student organization. b.
Activities of this nature, which are intellectually stimulating, must be well- planned, properly motivated by a genuine need to supplement regular curricular programs, and sponsored by an organization directly connected with the institution. c.
Persons to be invited as speakers shall be those who have distinguished themselves in their respective discipline or endeavor and shall contribute to the educational objectives of the University as well as the sponsoring organization. d.
Institution may withhold its approval when it has been established that the invited speaker is: i. a person who advocates or espouses the use of violence and disruptive measures to achieve his/her end; and/or ii. a person who has maliciously damaged the good name of the institution and its administration.

5.
Participation in Outside Activities a.
PnC (UC) students may participate in any outside activity-contest, play, band, exhibition games, symposium, society or group as representatives of the University, provided, that they have a written authorization from the SASD and VP SDAS and the Academic Head concerned. b.
Any recognized student organization that wishes to conduct a student activity outside the school premises should first seek formal approval from the SASD and VPSDAS. c.
All off-campus activities of recognized student organizations must be closely supervised by their respective advisers.
Activities sponsored and/or co-sponsored by any organization outside of the institution shall not be allowed without the approval of SASD and VPSDAS. d.
Parental consent (PNC:SDAS-FO-30) shall be issued by the SASD and accomplished and signed by the student and his/her parent or guardian. e.
Approved Absence Form (PNC:SDAS-FO-31) shall be secured by the concerned student/s to excuse him/her from attending to classes. f.
Faculty Conforme Form for Off-Campus Activity (PNC:SDAS-FO-32) shall be accomplished by the adviser or any delegated personnel, who will accompany the students in off-campus activities.
6.
Student Assembly a.
A student assembly shall mean convocation, symposium, seminar, workshop, procession, march, demonstration, rally, or any other form of meeting held by duly recognized student organizations in-person or virtually for such purposes as the discussion of issues, presentation of a lawful cause, expression of opinion, or petition for redress of grievances. b.

7.
Regular Meeting.
Recognized student organizations and student councils shall report to SASD for the updates about their respective organizations.
Regular meetings with student organizations quarterly or special meeting with the advisers shall be conducted by the SASD Director for closer coordination/ monitoring.
8.
Offenses and Sanctions a.
Any of the following circumstances are grounds for either suspension or withdrawal of recognition of a student organization by the SASD: i.
The organization violates its own constitution Sanction:
• First offense: written warning
• Second offense: suspension
• Third offense: withdrawal of recognition ii.
The organization fails to comply/follow the policies set by their department and the SASD: Sanction:
• First offense: written warning
• Second offense: final written warning
• Third offense: suspension
• Fourth offense: withdrawal of recognition iii.
The organization engaged in/supported subversive moves and other activities which are against the goals/policies of the institution
Sanction:
• First offense: withdrawal of recognition iv.
The organization fails to submit the required documents on time Sanction:
• First offense: written warning
• Second offense: final written warning
• Third offense: suspension
• Fourth offense: withdrawal of recognition v.

PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER VI PAMANTASAN NG CABUYAO STUDENT ELECTIONS > Section 1. General Policies
CHAPTER VI PAMANTASAN NG CABUYAO STUDENT ELECTIONS PNC:SDAS-GU-11 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
SASD through the SCOMELEC facilitates the Student Elections from the call for candidacy to the proclamation of winners guided by the principle that the University is a venue for the leadership development of the youth and that they have the right for organization and self-government.
2.
Composition, Qualifications, and Duties and Responsibilities of SCOMELEC a.
The SCOMELEC shall be composed of the Chairman and the Commissioners. b.
The SCOMELEC shall be composed of enrolled college and SHS students who are willing to take part in facilitating the student election except for the following: i.
Those who run for the specific position; ii.
Those who are incumbent officer for current year of election; and iii.
Those who have derogatory and disciplinary record. c.
Following are the duties and responsibilities of the SCOMELEC. i.
Oversee the planning, implementation, and evaluation of student election activities ii.
Ensure proper channeling and coordination of information and activities of the group iii.
Organizes student leadership colloquium or campaign forum and meeting de avance iv.
Ensures equal opportunities for all candidates during the event v.
Orients candidates of the Election Code, decorum, and
campaign rules vi.
Facilitates application for candidacy of individual or party vii.
Conducts screening of candidates viii.
Endorses qualified candidates ix.
Documents all election-related meetings and activities 3.
A one-day automated election every second semester shall be held for the student organizations and student council.
4.

Registration of Political Party a.

All political parties, however, are subject to screening of the SCOMELEC.
The following are the requirements necessary for the screening of the parties seeking for recognition: i.

Those who will be denied for candidacy shall be called by the SCOMELEC where the formal letter indicating the reasons shall be given and explained. e.
Those who were found eligible to pursue candidacy shall also be called by the SCOMELEC to officiate the Pledge of Honor and Commitment and the approval of candidacy by signing the COC. f.

passages.text:
PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER VI PAMANTASAN NG CABUYAO STUDENT ELECTIONS > Section 2. Specific Policies
All students who are interested to run and be elected for certain position in the organization must be in good academic standing i.e. have no failing grades in the last two semesters. ii.
The grades in Physical Education (PE) and National Service Training Program (NSTP) shall be considered in the computation of the weighted average.
The student should not have incurred a failure or dropped in any subject including PE and NSTP during the previous two semesters of their attendance. iii.
Probationary students are not allowed to run for any elective position.
Students who have record of any infraction inside or outside the school will not also be allowed to run for any elective position. iv.
Transferees should have at least two semesters of residency in the University before they will be allowed to run. v.
All the election processes of the academic and non-academic organizations shall be facilitated by the SCOMELEC. vi.
Candidates for elective position shall follow the rules and regulations set by the SCOMELEC on the process of elections. vii.
Once elected or appointed as an officer, the student must maintain a passing grade in all courses.
S/he must be of good moral character. viii.
Student leaders shall submit every semester to their adviser of the organization a photocopy of their compcard.
The SASD Director monitors the academic standing of the officers and recommends action to the VPSDAS. ix.
If the officer incurs a failing grade in any of the enrolled courses, s/he will be placed on probation.
If placed on probation, s/he will be given another semester to improve his/her grades.

If academic progress is not made after the prelim period of the succeeding semester, the individual will be required to resign from his/her position immediately. x.
In cases where there will be vacancy because of the previously mentioned reason, the organization's rule on
filling out of vacancy will be observed as mentioned in their respective constitution and by-laws. d.
Campaign Guidelines i.
All candidates are enjoined to engaged in wholesome and peaceful campaigning emphasis on merits as candidates and on what service the person or party may contribute for the welfare and betterment of all sectors of the institution. ii.
The campaign period shall take place three weeks before the actual election. iii.
Candidates and/or parties are prohibited from engaging in dirty or malicious campaign in any means that will impinge the honor and dignity of their fellow candidates or parties or the name of PNC (UC).
Acts that are inimical to a wholesome campaign are as follows: name calling, libelous accusations, false and grossly exaggerated claims devoid of material proofs, personal attacks on the private life/family of any candidate, destruction of campaign paraphernalia of other candidates or parties and vandalism in any form (social media, print, verbal, physical, etc). iv.
Participation in the campaign and election process is strictly limited in the students of PNC (UC).
Non-students, including alumni, are prohibited from meddling in the electoral process.
Parties and candidates are also prohibited from involving non-PNC (UC) students in the said activities. v.

passages.text:
PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER VI PAMANTASAN NG CABUYAO STUDENT ELECTIONS > Section 2. Specific Policies
Parties/individuals are prohibited from conducting boisterous and noisy forms of campaign in in-person or virtual University activities and spaces. vi.
Vote buying or any form of monetary inducement of voters is strictly prohibited.
Violation of this provision shall mean absolute disqualification. vii.
Coercion, harassment, intimidation of voters or candidates of another party is strictly prohibited. viii.
Candidates and/or parties shall be prohibited from enjoining teaching and non-teaching personnel on stating comments which may influence the voter's decision. ix.
Any violation in the prescribed campaign conduct shall be subjected to immediate disqualification if proven after due process of SCOMELEC
e.
Public Debate / Campaign Forum i.
A public debate may be organized by SCOMELEC for the contending parties and independent candidates aside from the traditional Meeting de Avance. ii.
The SCOMELEC shall act as moderator of the debate. f.
Canvassing of Votes i.
The canvassing of votes is automatic and the results are computer generated. ii.
For the canvassing process to be acknowledged as fair and honest, the parties are allowed to assign a maximum of two representatives to verify the election results. iii.
Candidates for each particular position who have received the most number of votes will be proclaimed the winner even if there is only one party running for election.
However, the candidate must receive 50% plus one vote of the total student population of the institution who voted for University Student Government and 50% plus one votes of the total student population who voted of their respective college/SHS. iv.

Should they reach an agreement, the SCOMELEC reserves the right to decide who the winner is after due process. g.
Proclamation i.
The proclamation of winners shall be made within the day of election upon the authenticated official printed result as acknowledged and signed by the SCOMELEC Officials, Party/Candidate Representative, SASD Director, and Vice President for Student Development and Auxiliary Services. ii.
The newly-elected officers shall be inducted before the start of the 1st semester of the following academic year.

h.
Election Complaints, Petitions, and Sanctions i.
All complaints, petitions, and sanctions shall be imposed, after due process, to any candidate/party that has committed any offenses. ii.
Complaints of a party/candidate against another party/ candidate arising from any violation of specific provisions in these guidelines shall be lodged before the SCOMELEC for preliminary investigation. iii.
Complaints, petitions, and sanctions shall be acted upon with due process.
Decisions shall be final and executory upon the concurrence of the SCOMELEC. iv.
Any defeated candidate or interested party may file an election protest with the SCOMELEC within one week after the receipt of the decision. v.
Violation of any provision of the guidelines shall render any candidate/party liable to appropriate penalty from SCOMELEC without prejudice to the sanctions to be given by the school authorities. i.
Failure of Election i.
In case of Failure of Election, an Alliance of Recognized Student Organization shall be formed by the SASD thru snap election.
Only the Presidents of the current student organizations can vote. ii.
The following may be considered as reasons for an election failure:
• No candidate signified interest to run in any or majority of number of positions both for USG, CSG and student councils
• Candidate/s did not receive 50% plus one votes.
• Massive election-related cheating. iii.
A snap election for Alliance of Recognized Student Organization shall be composed of all Presidents of the student organizations.

PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER VII GUIDANCE AND COUNSELING PROGRAM AND SERVICES > Section 2. Specific Policies
CHAPTER VII GUIDANCE AND COUNSELING PROGRAM AND SERVICES PNC:SDAS-GU-13 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
The Guidance and Counseling Department provides a comprehensive developmental guidance and counseling program which intends to develop well-functioning individuals and to ensure utilization of their fullest potentials.
2.
Suhay refers to support, which reflects the encompassing role of the Guidance and Counseling department in ensuring the academic, social, emotional and personal development of the students.
3.
PNC shall ensure confidentiality of all guidance and counseling student records.
Consent shall be secured by the Guidance and Counseling Department to all concerned counselee.
However, records may be released to concerned department under certain circumstances: a.
If the student/personnel present/presents a serious danger to self or other person(s); b.
If there is a suspicion or actual incident of abuse or neglect; c.
Presence of a valid subpoena is issued for concerned student/ personnel records, or d.
Student/personnel records are otherwise subject to a court order or other legal process requiring disclosure.
Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
The following are the guidance services provided to all students and personnel of Pamantasan ng Cabuyao
a.
Individual Inventory Service. i.
This maintains a record of students' study habits, health and well-being, personality assessment, career questionnaire, counseling sessions, scholastic progress, and other data relevant to their development and progress in TVL, senior, college, and graduate school.

passages.page_or_section: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER VII GUIDANCE AND COUNSELING PROGRAM AND SERVICES > Section 2. Specific Policies (pp. 164-165)
passages.text:
PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER VII GUIDANCE AND COUNSELING PROGRAM AND SERVICES > Section 2. Specific Policies
Basic inquiries about family and education shall be maintained at the Office of the University Registrar through a centralized student information system. ii.
Student Cumulative Record (PNC:SDAS-FO-36) is filled out by the students online or via google forms before the semester ends.
This applies to all new or first year students.
For continuing education students, PNC:SDAS-FO-37 shall be accomplished by the students online or via google forms. b.
Counseling Service. i.
The counseling services provide assistance to students in making decision about their problems.
The following counseling sessions are made available for all students with academic, personal, interpersonal, career concerns and other problems affecting them.
These may be done online or remote.
• Individual Counseling/e-Counseling.
A one-on-one session between counselor and counselee.
• Group Counseling.
This service is intended for students to share a common need or concern that is usually developmental in nature
• Exit Interview.
Exiting students (graduating and transferees) shall undergo exit interview before signing their clearance.
Exit Interview Form (PNC:SDAS-FO-38) shall be distributed to student leavers. ii.
Counseling Session Report Form (PNC:SDAS-FO-39) shall be accomplished to document the results of the counseling session. iii.
An Informed Consent Form (PNC:SDAS-FO-40) shall be
accomplished and duly signed by the counselee, parent/ guardian (for below 18 years old counselee) and the counselor prior to start of any counseling sessions.
This allows counselee to become partners in assessing best possible management that accord with their own needs and values. iv.

Following are the responsibilities of the counselee
• Take an active role in the counseling process and working toward the goals set by the counselor.
If it is determined that the counselee is not working towards identified goals, the counseling relationship may be terminated.
• Come to scheduled appointments on time.
Tardiness of 15 minutes or more for a scheduled appointment will mean rescheduling of the counseling session.
• Call and cancel appointment if counselee will not be able to come.
For two or more "no shows," it will be assumed that the counselee is no longer interested in counseling and will be removed from the schedule.
• Excessive tardiness (three or more late arrivals) will mean forfeiture of counseling services.
Two or more cancellations will mean that I/my child will be removed from the schedule. c.

Follow-up Service.
This is to determine the success or failure of the counseling session/s conducted online or in-person.
Further, students who were referred due to academic failure shall be called for academic follow-up by the counselor. e.
Career Development Service.
In coordination with the Placement, Alumni, and Linkages Department, these
activities intend to attain competencies needed to prepare for meaningful, satisfying, and productive career of PnC (UC) students. f.
Enhancement Program i.

This test helps students identify their career aptitudes and interests and find careers that align with their strengths ii.
Grade 12 – Career Orientation Placement and Evaluation Survey (COPES).
This test intends to measure personal values in the workplace.
This will help students to find occupational areas that match their personal values. iii.
First Year College – Scholastic Ability Test for Adults (SATA).
This test is designed to measure scholastic competence of the student to highlight individual strengths, weaknesses and areas of competence iv.
Second Year College – Occupational Aptitude Survey and Interest Schedule (OASIS-3).
This test helps students identify their career aptitudes and interests and find careers that align with their strengths. v.
Third Year – Manchester Personality Test.
This test is designed to identify and report on key personality traits likely to have a high impact on behavior and success at work and to highlight individual strengths, weaknesses and areas of competence. vi.
Fourth Year – Career Attitudes and Strategies Inventory (CASI) and BarOn Emotional Quotient Test for internship students, CASI will assess students' likelihood of job stability or change, potential career obstacles, or areas for further development.
Meanwhile, BarOn measures the emotional and social behavior of students. vii.
Graduate School Students – BarOn Emotional Quotient Test and MD5 Mental Ability Test.
The latter is designed to assess the students' ability to use logic and reasoning to solve cryptic problems, under a tight time pressure.

PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER VIII ALUMNI PROGRAM AND SERVICES > Section 2. Specific Policies
CHAPTER VIII ALUMNI PROGRAM AND SERVICES PNC:SDAS-GU-14 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
The Placement, Alumni, and Linkage Department shall facilitate the alumni programs and services.
2.
The PALD Director shall collaborate with the Alumni Regent in carrying out the activities outlined in this guideline.
3.
PALD shall mobilize Placement, Alumni, and Linkage Coordinator for each academic department.
They shall assist PALD Director in all aspects of alumni relations delivery.
Appointment paper shall be issued by the Vice President for Student Development and Auxiliary Services upon endorsement by the PALD Director.
Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
Alumni Tracking. a.
In order to track alumni, the Alumni Profile Tracer Form must be completed (PNC:SDAS-FO-41).
The form mentioned above can be filled out in a variety of ways, including in person at the university, via email, social media, and other online platforms. b.
The report on alumni tracking will be forwarded to the Research and Development Department for analysis and interpretation.
2.
Alumni Placement a.
The Office shall manage career development service, including placement activities and Career Fair for graduating students.
These include job posting, in-campus/remote recruitment, among others.
This intend to increase the basic
career competencies, employability, and personal skills of the graduating students. b.
These activities shall be conducted in coordination with the Guidance and Counseling Department.
3.
Collection of Alumni Fee.
Alumni Fee shall be collected yearly.
4.
Processing and Distributing Alumni Cards a.
The alumni card serves to identify University alumni. b.

Following graduation, members of the Senior High School, Collegiate Departments, and Graduate School receive the aforementioned alumni card. c.
PALD manages the printing of alumni cards in collaboration with the Office of the University Registrar for the official list of graduates. d.
The Office of the University Registrar will facilitate the distribution of alumni cards, along with the diploma and transcript of record.
If the printing of the alumni cards is delayed, alumni may claim them at PALD. e.
Alumni who graduated prior to the implementation of the alumni card may request a copy (PNC:SDAS-FO-42).
Additionally, alumni who have lost or damaged their alumni card may request a replacement by submitting a duly-notarized affidavit of loss. f.
PALD may collaborate with shop owners or institutions to establish Alumni Card rewards and privileges.
5.
Monitoring of Alumni Activities a.
The University's alumni welcome-back event is called "PAG-UWI".
It can be an annual grand reunion of alumni or reunion held every five years.
This will be held during the PNC (UC) Foundation Celebration.

passages.text:
PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER IX LIBRARY SERVICES > Section 1. General Policies
CHAPTER IX LIBRARY SERVICES PNC:AA-GU-16 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
Library Service Hours.
The library is open from Mondays to Fridays from 8am-5pm.
Schedules are adjusted based on the academic calendar of the University.
During Saturdays, graduate school needs shall be attended by the Library.
2.
Access to the Library a.
The library is open to all bonafide students, teaching and non-teaching personnel of the University. b.
Alumni and outside researchers may avail themselves of the resources subject to the rules and regulations of the library. c. eLibrary can be accessed by the students, teaching and non-teaching personnel, and outside researchers anytime, anywhere. d.
The University Library shall enforce all national and local government laws relative to any related health-posing-risk situations. e.
University students, teaching, and non-teaching personnel. i.
Personal belongings shall be deposited at the depository shelf at the entrance of the library. ii.
Library clients must bring with them their valuables such as money, jewelry, and cellular phones.
The library will not be held liable for lost valuables. iii.
Clients may use any material, shelved, or stores in the stack areas, and any equipment or facilities that are designated for use except where restrictions are established by the
library; iv.
Upon entrance, library clients are required to present their school ID. v.
Upon entering the library, the clients must log using a Library Monitoring System.
It collects the following details:
• Date of Visit;
• Name;
• ID Number; and
• Program/Department. f.
Alumni and Outside Researchers. i.

Graduates of the University may access and use the library upon presentation of the Alumni Card or other proof of identity. ii.
In the absence of an Alumni Card, a referral letter from the University Librarian of the institution s/he is currently enrolled or from a designated manager of the company s/ he is working must be presented. iii.
Alumni and outside researchers are allowed to do face-to-face research during Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturdays from 9am-4pm, except on declared non-working holidays and exam week.
As to access with eLibrary, a validity of 1 day access will be given. iv.
Alumni and outside researchers shall pay Php 50.00 at the Cashier's Office before using the library facilities and resources.
After payment, the researcher shall present the official receipt to the Library Staff for recording purposes. v.
Upon entrance, library clients are required to present their valid ID. vi.
Upon entering the library, the clients must log using a Library Monitoring System.
It collects the following details:
• Date of Visit;
• Name;
• Program (if applicable); and
• School/Company.

3.
Library Users Conduct and Study Atmosphere a.
The following shall be permitted at the University Library: i.
Tablet, CD players and similar gadgets with earphones provided volume is kept low; ii.
Use of cellular phones is allowed, however, it is expected that ring tones must be on silent mode and calls should be done outside the library. iii.
Use of laptop, which requires electric consumption. iv.
Scanning of theses abstracts through mobile phones or similar gadget v.
Quiet study: Users are allowed to study in designated quiet areas of the library without disturbing others. vi.
Group study: Users may engage in group study in designated areas of the library, as long as they do not disturb others. b.
The following activities shall not be permitted at the University Library: i.
Disruptive behavior.
Any behavior that creates a disturbance, including loud talking, laughing, cell phone use, disorderly conversation, and other disruptive activities, is not allowed. ii.
Vandalism and theft.
Any activity that damages or destroys library resources or property, including theft of library materials, is strictly prohibited. iii.
Inappropriate use of computers and internet resources.
Users are not allowed to use library computers and internet resources for illegal or inappropriate activities, including accessing inappropriate or offensive content. iv.
Eating meals.
Users are not allowed to eat meals in the library, as this may create a disturbance and damage library resources. v.
Borrowing or using ID of others; vi.
Gross discourtesy or acts of disrespect to any library personnel; vii.
Mutilation or defacement of library materials, including marking pages with pens, highlighters, or other
instruments, folding, tearing or removal of pages, purposely damaging materials or any other library property; viii.

Concealment or hiding of library materials in any area of the library for one's exclusive use; x.
Scanning, photographing or taking pictures of the entire theses; xi.
Loitering, running, blocking, or interfering with the free movement of other individuals; xii.
Harassing, threatening, or showing unlawful and violent behavior to other library users; xiii.
Playing cards or any other forms of gambling 4.

Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
Activation of Library Account.
At the start of the school year, the Library shall facilitate the account activation through the eLibrary.
2.
Loan Period a.
Students i.
Students are allowed to borrow a maximum of three books for home loan overnight or fiction book for seven days at any given time.
Books are released starting 11:00 in the morning. ii.
Borrowed books shall be returned on or before 10:00 am of the next school day. iii.
Borrowed books shall be returned first before they can borrow another book at the least or two at the most.
These may be renewed provided there is no prior reservation
request for the borrowed book. iv.

Reference books (almanac, atlas, dictionary, directory, encyclopedias, gazetteer, geographical dictionary, handbook, and manual), periodicals/journals, newly acquired book and Audio-Visual Materials are for room use only but may be borrowed for one hour for photocopying purposes. v.
No more than two periodicals may be borrowed for photocopying at any given time. vi.
Students may borrow undergraduate theses, feasibility studies and the like for library reading room use only at any given time. vii.
Students may borrow multimedia materials but these are to be used inside the Library only. viii.
Student assistant assigned in the library are given privilege to borrow three books for a week instead of two days only. ix.
No overnight loans are issued during the first and last two weeks of the semester. b.
Teaching and non-teaching personnel i.
Teaching and non-teaching personnel are allowed to borrow a maximum of five library materials including circulation and multimedia materials for seven days and these may be renewed twice provided there is no prior reservation request. ii.
Teaching and non-teaching personnel are allowed to borrow two back issues of periodicals every Friday and must be returned on Monday of the following week. iii.
Teaching and non-teaching personnel are allowed to borrow reference, reserve book, current periodicals, theses, dissertations, and the like for room use and photocopying only at any given time.
The research abstracts can be downloaded from the eLibrary. c.

3.
Online Public Access Catalog (OPAC) a.
The Library has digital card catalog which serves as an index to the books. b.
Non-fiction books are arranged on the shelves by the call numbers. c.
Fiction book has call number and is arranged alphabetically on the shelves by the author's last name.
4.
Borrowing Library Materials a.
All library privileges are granted only to the person named on the official ID of Pamantasan ng Cabuyao. b.
Borrowers shall fill out the Book Card (PNC:AA-FO-40) with their name and ID number.
This shall be presented together to the Library Staff at the Circulation Desk for proper recording at the eLibrary. c.
Library Staff shall note the due date on the book card and eLibrary. d.
Library staff shall file book card alphabetically based on the borrower's name. e.
Overdue materials shall be returned and overdue fines shall be paid first before they may be borrowed.
Payment shall be made at the Cashier's Office.
It shall be remitted as a subsidiary account for the use of the University Library. f.
Borrowing privileges shall be suspended until overdue accounts have been settled 5.
Returning Library Materials a.
Library user shall present the library materials to the library staff at the Circulation Counter. b.
The Library Staff shall retrieve the book card from the file, note the return date, and affix the initials on the book card.

c.
Library staff shall insert the book card in the book pocket. d.
Library staff shall shelve the library materials. e.
If the library material is overdue, the Library staff shall issue payment slip and report may be generated from the eLibrary system. f.
Library user shall pay the overdue fine at the Cashier's Office present the Official Receipt to the library staff after payment. g.
The eLibrary monitors the delinquency of borrowers.
It shall indicate if it is the first or last offense notice on the students' record regarding their accountabilities.
6.
Renewal of Borrowed Library Materials a.
Library materials are renewable unless there is prior reservation. b.
Library materials may be renewed through eLibrary 7.
Reservation of Library Materials a.
If the library materials are loaned out, borrowers may request for the reservation through eLibrary or personal visit on first come first serve basis. b.
Once the book is returned, the Library Staff shall inform the person who requested the book for reservation or on hold.
If after two days, the requester fails to borrow the book, the Library Staff shall lend or shelve it.
8.
Issuance of Recall Letter a.
A recall letter is issued to borrowers with delinquent accounts through their Deans/Principal at least two weeks past overdue.

b.
The Library shall forward the list of students and teaching and non-teaching personnel with the Dean/Principal/Chair at least two weeks prior to ending of the semester.
9.
Fines and Penalties of Library Materials a.
Failure to return the books and other library materials on its due date is charged Php 20.00 per day per title for undergraduate and Php 50.00 for graduate students including Saturday, Sundays and holidays and may incur the following penalties:
• 1st Offense: Verbal warning and payment of appropriate fine
• 2nd Offense: Payment of appropriate fine/penalty charges and suspension of library privileges for one week
• 3rd Offense: Payment of appropriate fine/penalty charges and suspension of library privileges for the rest of the semester. b.
Fraction of a day shall be considered one full day. c.
The penalties shall continue to accumulate on all overdue materials until the item is renewed, returned, or is declared lost by borrowers.
10.
Lost and Replacement Charges of Library Materials a.
Lost books shall be reported to the Library immediately by the borrower. b.
Reported lost book shall be replaced with the same title and author with the latest edition by the borrower 11.
Processing of Clearance a.
The library staff shall check the borrower's library account. b.
If the borrower is cleared of accountabilities, the library staff shall clear him/her through the eLibrary.

12.
Library Education Program.
Library provides orientation to all students during the opening of classes.
13.
Computer / Gadget Use Services a.
The school ID shall be presented each time the computer or gadget shall be used. b.
Any malfunction or damage in the computers or gadgets shall be reported immediately to the library staff on duty. c.
The internet service and use of computers/gadget shall be used within the academic context i.e. research, education, and study purposes only. d.
Use of computer/gadget shall be on a first come first served basis.
A maximum of two hours will be allowed in one session for every student.
Saving files in the computer/gadget shall not be allowed. e.
In the event of loss or theft of computer and its peripherals and other gadgets, the Library shall: i.
Immediately report the incident to the Security Office; ii.
Trace the last user of the terminal; iii.
Make an incident report and submit to the University Librarian; iv.
Conduct an initial investigation; and v.
Write an investigation report and submit it to the appropriate department f.
Flash drives may only be plugged in-on designated computers.
14.
Charges for Damaged Materials.
A fee is charged for materials that are damaged while on loan or use in the Library.
Disciplinary action will be taken against any student who intentionally damage library materials.
To determine the charges, the following applies a.
Minor Damage/s are damage/s with a few pencil marks, bent pages, and slight water damage.

Sanction: Stern warning with no fee b.

Major Damage/s to cover and binding require extensive repairs.

Gathering of Client Satisfaction Responses.
All services shall be evaluated by the clients thru the QR code to be sent by the Library Staff via email or any platform.
16.
Library Committee a.
The Library Committee aims the following: i.
To provide oversight and guidance for library operations: The Library Committee serves as a governing body that oversees and guides the operation of the library, ensuring that it is meeting the needs of the University's community and operating in line with its philosophy and objectives ii.
To ensure that the library's collection is current, relevant, and diverse: The Library Committee helps to guide collection development decisions, including the selection and acquisition of materials, to ensure that the library's collection is meeting the needs of its users and is up-to-date with the latest trends and developments in various fields. iii.

To provide high-quality user services: The Library Committee helps to develop and review library services, including reference services, instruction programs, and interlibrary loan services, to ensure that they are meeting
the needs of library users and are providing high-quality support for learning, teaching, and research. iv.
To ensure that the library is effectively utilizing its resources: The Library Committee helps to allocate resources for library operations, including budgeting and staffing decisions, to ensure that the library is effectively utilizing its resources to meet the needs of its users. v.
To promote the library's resources and services to the institution's community, including students, faculty, and staff, and to engage in outreach efforts to promote the library's mission and services to the wider community. vi.
To support research activity for its progress and qualitative development b.
The Library Committee has the following duties and responsibilities: i.
To serve as the channel of communication between the library and their faculty and students relating to library events. ii.
To assist in acquiring and selecting library materials through book and other library materials selection activities. iii.
To participate in the collection development in accordance with the library collection analysis report. iv.
To help the library its promotional activities. v.
To participate in the revisions of the library's policies and programs vi.
To prepare and submit to the Academic Council, semestral report summarizing the activities and achievements of the library. vii.
To work towards modernization and improvement of Library Services. c.

CHAPTER X MEDICAL AND DENTAL SERVICES PNC:AF-GU-01 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
The University shall maintain a University Health Department (UHD) that address the medical and dental needs of the University.
2.
The UHD shall be manned by professionals duly registered and recognized by the Professional Regulation Commission.
3.
The UHD is open from Monday to Friday, 8am to 5pm.
If there are classes beyond regular office hours, schedule will be adjusted accordingly.
4.
To ensure that the University's students and teaching and non-teaching personnel are at the best of their health, especially when they participate in any sports event, the UHD shall hold annual medical and dental examinations.
5.
Only medical and dental personnel duly recognized by the University shall perform the annual medical and dental examinations and consultations.
6.
Only those sick patients shall be allowed to stay at the UHD.
Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
On Routine Medical and Dental Examinations a.

CHAPTER XI CLIENT SATISFACTION SURVEY PNC:PRE-GU-05 Section 1.
General Policies 1.

The comments and suggestions to be raised by the clients present customer needs and expectation.

2.
Comments and suggestion will also be gathered from the clients..
3.
The PNC CSS information system organize, classify, and present in tabular/graphical forms the collected data.
These are made accessible to all departments and offices.
4.
QMPD shall present the results of the Client Satisfaction Survey (CSS) report to the Management Committee monthly.

passages.text:
PART 4. CODE OF CONDUCT AND DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES
Welcome to the Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedures section of the Student Manual.
At Pamantasan ng Cabuyao, we believe in fostering a safe, inclusive, and respectful learning environment for all members of our community.
This section outlines the expectations, rights, and responsibilities that guide our interactions and behaviors as students.
The Code of Conduct serves as a framework that upholds our institution's values, promotes ethical conduct, and ensures the well-being of everyone on campus.
It sets forth the standards of behavior that we expect from each student, emphasizing integrity, honesty, respect, and accountability.
In addition to the Code of Conduct, this section provides you with an overview of the disciplinary procedures in place to address violations of the Code.
These procedures are designed to be fair, transparent, and aimed at promoting learning, growth, and corrective action when necessary.
It is important to familiarize yourself with these procedures to understand your rights and the consequences associated with any misconduct.
We believe in the power of education to transform lives, and our commitment to a positive and respectful community is at the heart of that belief.
As a student at PnC, you have the responsibility to uphold the values outlined in the Code of Conduct and contribute to an inclusive and safe environment for yourself and your fellow students.
Remember, the Code of Conduct is not just a set of rules; it is a commitment to shared values and principles that shape our collective experience as students.
Let us embrace these guidelines as we embark on our journey of learning, growth, and community at PnC.

CHAPTER I CODE OF STUDENT CONDUCT PNC:SDAS-GU-04 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
Students are required to conduct themselves and dress appropriately at all times in accordance with the rules established by the university.
2.
Parents, guardians, and/or students are required to become familiar with the information in this guideline.
Any student is nonetheless subject to the consequences listed here even if they are unaware of the rules contained here.
3.
Students must be proud of their university and act in a way that upholds the reputation of the institution no matter where they are.
4.
Students are expected to conduct themselves in a mature and responsible manner at all times, on and off campus, by respecting those in positions of authority, upholding the rights of their fellow students, and upholding the reputation of the university.
The administration may recommend appropriate action after due process if a student's general behavior, including but not limited to social media, throws the university's rules and regulations into question.
Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
Proper Grooming a.
Proper grooming includes wearing the required uniform, the acceptable shoes, the ID, the male hairstyle, and other comparable issues. i.
Uniform.
In-person classes require students to wear the required uniform, unless the Student Affairs and Services
Department has given an exception (SASD). ii.
For in-person classes, working students may be exempted from wearing their school uniform, provided they present the following documents to SASD:
• photocopy of official enrollment form
• 1 copy of 1x1 recent picture
• Request for Uniform Exemption and Gate Pass (PNC:SDAS-FO-09)

Micro-mini skirts (more than 3 inches from the kneecap), short shorts, cycling pants, tube, sleeveless, plunging neckline blouses, see-through blouses, halter tops, backless tops, tank tops, leggings, sandos, sleeveless jerseys, and slippers are considered inappropriate flexible learning attire.

CHAPTER II STUDENT DISCIPLINE PNC:SDAS-GU-05 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
Disciplinary actions are corrective measures imposed on students who failed to comply with the provisions on the expected student decorum.
The primary objective of these actions is to guide the erring students to follow the path of right conduct.
Severe disciplinary actions, however, may be imposed on certain cases as the circumstances may warrant.
2.
The imposition of the appropriate disciplinary action shall be progressive in character, taking into account the previous violations committed by the offender.
If the offender was already warned because of a minor offense that he/she committed, a second violation involving the same minor offense or a more serious offense shall be meted suspension/ non-readmission/exclusion/ expulsion depending on the gravity of the offense. a.
A Reprimand shall serve as a warning (PNC:SDAS-FO-10) that any future violation of this guideline shall be a ground for the imposition of a more severe penalty. b.
A Warning is a written notice (PNC:SDAS-FO-10) to the offender that continuation or repetition of the wrongful conduct within a period of time stated in the warning may be a cause for more severe disciplinary action. c.
A Suspension is a penalty in which a student is denied or deprived of attendance in classes which shall be imposed for serious or major offenses or willful violations of this guideline.
Serious or major offenses may warrant the imposition of a longer duration of suspension for the student concerned, which could range from a whole term to an entire academic year, as the assigned Panel for the case would deem appropriate and just.

A Restitution refers to reimbursement for a damage to or misappropriation of property; this may take the form of appropriate repair service or damage compensation. iv.
Non-readmission is a penalty that allows the institution to deny admission or enrollment of an erring student for the school term immediately following the term when the resolution or decision finding the student guilty of the offense charged and imposing the penalty of non-readmission was promulgated.
Unlike the penalty of exclusion, the student is allowed to complete the current school term when the resolution of non-readmission was promulgated.
Transfer of credentials of the erring student shall be issued upon promulgation, subject to the other provisions of the M.O.R.P.H.E. v.
Exclusion is a penalty that allows the institution to exclude or drop the name of the erring student from the rolls of students immediately upon resolution for exclusion was promulgated.

3.
The University may compel students to keep the norms of conduct expected of members of the academic community, whether on or off campus.
Therefore, when students misbehave outside the campus and the misconduct complained of directly affects the offender's status as a suitable member of that community, there is no reason why the school may not impose disciplinary sanctions on him.
4.
Sanctions may also be imposed on students who, after due process, were found to be accomplices and accessories to an offense.
5.
The imposition of the disciplinary sanctions for the violation of any rule under this guideline shall not preclude the University from endorsing the case to proper government authorities when the same may involve violations of penal laws.
6.
When the violation is perpetrated by non-bonafide students within the University with the cooperation or participation of Pamantasan ng Cabuyao students, the latter shall be responsible for the acts of the former.
7.
Discipline of recognized/accredited student organizations i.
Reprimand shall serve as a warning that any future violation of this Code shall be a ground for the imposition of a more severe penalty. ii.
Suspension which could range from several days to an entire academic year or longer depending on the gravity of the offense.
The types of suspension are:
• Suspension of activities.
• Suspension from operations.
• Suspension of certain rights and privileges to be specified by the SDB such as use of University facilities, non-approval of budget, subsidy in activities, etc.

Once caught for a specific violation, the concerned personnel or student shall inform the offender about the nature of his/her violation. ii.
A referral slip (PNC:SDAS-FO-13) shall be prepared and submitted by the concerned personnel or student to the SASD.
The latter shall fill up the said form.
Details shall be verified with the student ID or registration form. iii.
Student offender shall be advised to report immediately to the SASD for appropriate action.
9.
Handling Disciplinary Cases i.
Disciplinary actions shall be imposed only after due process has been observed. ii.
The PnC-UC Student Discipline Board (SDB) is mandated to hear and decide on serious or major disciplinary cases of students. iii.
Composition of the Student Discipline Board (SDB)
• Director for Student Affairs and Services Department (Chair)
• Administrator Representative.
S/he must have no direct relationship with the parties involved; does not belong to the same department as the charged student
• Full-time Teaching Personnel Representative.
S/he must have no direct relationship with the parties involved.
• Student Representative.
S/he may not be an elected officer of the student council or any recognized student organization; no direct relationship with the parties involved; no derogatory record; should be at least third year in standing; does not belong to the same department as the charged student
• Student Discipline Officer (Secretary)

iv.
Responsibilities of the Student Discipline Board
• Director for Student Affairs and Services Department (Chair)
• Act as presiding officer of the board
• Spearheads all the hearings and meetings of the board
• Has the authority to control the conduct of all persons present during the hearings
• Observes procedural matters such as length of time for hearing, breaks, personal commitments of board members
• Asks both the complainant and the respondent to present evidence and permits the defendant to cross-examine witness
• Prepares the final report at the conclusion of the hearing.
• Administrator Representative, Faculty Representative, Student Representative
• Attends and participates in all the hearings and meetings of the board
• Listens to the testimonies of the witnesses and weights the evidences presented
• Asks questions for clarifications anytime during the hearing
• Gives his/her verdict during the final deliberation of the case
• Student Discipline Officer
• Prepares the minutes of the board hearings and meetings
• Assists the Chair in drafting the final report of the case decision v.
Under no circumstances shall an SDB be handling more than three cases in the same semester.
In such cases, the SASD Director has to constitute another SDB to handle other cases.

vi.
All cases shall be resolved by the SDB within the semester, when the SDB is constituted. vii.
Procedure in convening the board and the case promulgation
• Upon receipt of the written accusation, the Student Discipline Officer shall issue a show cause notice informing the student-respondent/s of the nature and cause of accusation and shall require him/her/them to answer the accusation in writing within 5 days from receipt thereof.
If the student is a minor, the parent or guardian shall be furnished with a copy of the show cause notice.
• The student-respondent/s shall be informed of the evidence against him/her/them and he/she/they shall have the right to adduce evidence on his/her/their behalf.
• Upon receipt of the answer or should the student/s fail to submit his/her/their answer within the given period, the Student Discipline Officer shall set the case for preliminary investigation to clarify the facts and/or to give the student another opportunity to be heard.
• All communications to the offender and accused shall be sent in person.
Otherwise, it shall be processed thru registered mail.
• The Student Discipline Officer shall submit a recommendation, together with the preliminary investigation report, to the SASD Director if a serious or major case is filed at the Office.
The Student Discipline Board shall be convened within seven days thereafter.
• The preliminary investigation report shall be submitted with the following contents but not limited to:
• Written complaint and evidences
• Written explanation of the respondent and evidences
• Background of the complainant and respondent (Academic record, disciplinary record, biodata, among others)

• In-depth interview result of the parties involved

• The Student Discipline Officer shall recommend to the SASD Director the members of the Student Discipline Board.
Names shall be endorsed to the Vice President for Student Development and Auxiliary Services for approval.
Appointment paper shall be prepared by VPSDAS.
• The SASD Director shall meet the members of the board for the orientation and to discuss the case.
S/he shall schedule the SDB meetings and hearings.
The board members, the complainant, respondent, and their respective witnesses shall be given written notice on the schedule of the hearings.
• The SDB shall consider the evidence, write the facts and issue a resolution.
The Chair, with the assistance of the Secretary, shall make the Case Decision Report duly signed by all members of the SDB.
The said resolution shall be endorsed by the SASD Director to the Vice President for Student Development and Auxiliary Services for approval.
• The complainant and the respondent shall be given a written copy of the decision.
• The approved resolution shall be final and executory unless stayed by SASD within 10 days from date of promulgation.
• The respondent may appeal on the decision by writing a formal letter for reconsideration addressed to the University President within three working days upon receipt of the decision.
• The decision on the appeal shall be communicated in writing and shall be considered final and irrevocable.
