CHAPTER III STUDENT GRIEVANCE PNC:SDAS-GU-06 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
Grievance against any member of the PnC-UC community should be initially settled with the person concerned through sincere dialogue and discussion.
2.
If, for whatever reason, a student/s does/do not wish to communicate directly with the concerned person to discuss his/her complaint or grievance, he/she should file a written complaint with the Program Chair or Dean/Principal who has supervision over the teaching personnel for academic-related concerns.
Non-academic-related concerns shall be filed at the Student Affairs and Services Department.
3.
It is only when the initial discussion fails that one may resort to formal procedure for settling offense / complaints.
4.
A case conference shall be conducted to resolve grievances.
First option is to settle the case amicably between parties involved.
Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
All complaints shall be addressed by the concerned office.
For example: a.
Issues about academic probations shall be handled by the Office of the Dean/Principal. b.
Issues about the performance or behavior of the support staff shall be lodged with the Human Resource Management Department of the University. c.
Issues about possible crimes etc. shall be filed with the Student Affairs and Services Department d.
Regarding issues about health, the student shall contact the University Health Department
e.
Issues about scholarships, financial aid, etc. shall be handled by the Student Affairs and Services Department 2.

If the student feels that he/she does not receive the necessary actions on his/her complaint from the respective offices, the case may be referred to Student Affairs and Services Department.
3.
In case the student brings his/her grievance to the University Student Government (USG), the USG officers may refer the student to the SASD for appropriate action.
4.
If the grievance is not written, the SASD Director shall request the student to write a formal complaint against the subject of the grievance.
5.
In extreme cases when the evidence gathered is substantial that a violation of the guideline occurred, the SASD may initiate preliminary investigation despite the absence of a written complaint.
6.
If the SASD Director finds merit in the case, he/she shall endorse the case to the concerned Dean/Principal if it is a student and teaching personnel related complaint.
He/she shall conduct an investigation following the requirements of due process.
7.
The SASD Director shall then recommend to the VPSDAS the particular course of action concerning the parties involved.
8.
If the case constitutes a serious and major offense, the SASD Director may recommend the convening of the Student Discipline Board to decide on the matter.
9.
A student shall follow the specific procedures for formal complaints: a.
Student's Complaints against Another Student i.
The complainant must submit a written complaint against the student respondent at the SASD ii.
The SASD Director has three (3) to five (5) working days to act on the complaint.

Student's Complaints against a Teaching Personnel i.
Issues about grades, examinations, excused absences, class policies, etc. shall be resolved under the following considerations:
• Teaching personnel have primary responsibility in all these areas and are charged with carrying out those responsibilities in a professional manner and in accordance with the policies issued by the University.
• The Dean/Principal, in coordination with the Program Chair, has the authority and responsibility to deal with changes of grades in special cases such as those which might involve the teaching personnel who have left the university or unprofessional teaching personnel conduct in assigning the grade.
• Student/s should be aware that neither the Program Chair nor the Dean/Principal can require a teaching personnel to change a properly assigned course grade.
• Issues of disagreement about answers to test questions are decided solely by the teaching personnel.

CHAPTER IV CONDUCT OF DRUG TESTING PNC:SDAS-GU-07 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
Through the Student Affairs and Services Department, the University must create a Drug-Free Committee (DFC).
The DFC is responsible for developing and putting into action drug testing policies, which include programs for drug prevention, control, and education.
Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
Notification a.
Before full implementation, Pamantasan ng Cabuyao shall inform the school community of the prescribed guidelines and ensure that they are included in the Student Manual with proper notice to all students and parents on the procedure and manner in which the random drug testing shall be conducted.
The administration of the drug test shall not be prevented by the failure to return the acknowledgment receipt. b.
Through the University Student Government, students will be consulted about the mandated drug testing procedure.
The consultation process must be completed by the end of February of the academic year prior to the one in which the planned mandatory testing will take place.
2.
Samples a.
The random sampling includes every student enrolled at the institution. b.
The quantity of samples need to result in a 95% statistical confidence level for the entire student body.

c.
To determine the number of students who will be subject to random drug testing, the Drug-Free Committee (DFC) will employ Slovin's formula.
3.
Selection of Samples a.
The School Nurse shall serve as the Drug Testing Coordinator.
S/he shall convene the Drug-Free Committee within five (5) days from the receipt of notice.
The Drug-Free Committee shall be composed of the following: i.
Director, Student Affairs and Services Department (Chair); ii.
Full-time Teaching Personnel Representative; iii.
Parent Representative; iv.
Student Representative; v.
University Health Department Representative; and vi.
Student Discipline Officer (Secretary). b.
The Drug-Free Committee will administer a random selection of those to be tested on the testing day. c.
The drug-free committee will make sure the random selection method is fair and impartial. d.
The selection procedure will be done at random using a lottery that may be computerized or in any other way that the committee may decide. e.
Students will be chosen at random and tested for drugs on the same day.
The list of the chosen students and their class schedule will be sent to the student discipline officer, who will then go to their classrooms to collect them or send an online invitation before heading straight to the University Health Department. f.
The chosen students will be questioned about any prescription medications, vitamins, or food supplements they have taken during the last five (5) days before the test.
The Drug Testing Coordinator must preserve the list and refer to it when assessing the results of the confirmatory drug test.

The results of the test shall be strictly confidential.
The University shall not publish or post results whether positive or negative. b.

In case the results are positive at the screening level, the same specimen shall immediately be submitted for confirmation observing all strict chain of custody procedures and confidentiality of records. d.
If a student is "confirmed" to be using a dangerous drug, the following shall be observed. i.
The University Health Department receives an official report from the laboratory in a sealed envelope. ii.
The SASD shall inform the parent and the student of the results and how the information is regarded with utmost secrecy and confidentiality.

CHAPTER V SOCIAL MEDIA GUIDELINE PNC:AF-GU-28 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
The purpose of social media use is to effectively engage and communicate with stakeholders, including students, personnel, alumni, and the general public.
2.
Social media can enhance the University's reputation and visibility, share news and updates, promote events and activities, facilitate dialogue and conversation, and provide valuable resources and information to the community.
3.
It can also be used for recruitment, retention, fundraising efforts, as well as for research and academic purposes.
4.
All personnel and students of the University are expected to use social media responsibly, ethically, and professionally, consistent with the University' philosophy and objectives. a.
Professionalism: All personnel and students of the University should maintain a professional tone and demeanor when using social media.
This includes refraining from profanity, discriminatory language, personal attacks, or other unprofessional behavior. b.
Confidentiality: All personnel and students of the University must maintain confidentiality and protect the privacy of the organization, its clients, and stakeholders.
This means refraining from sharing confidential information, trade secrets, or other sensitive information through social media channels. c.
Respect for others: All personnel and students of the University should treat others with respect, civility, and courtesy.
This includes refraining from engaging in bullying, harassment, or other forms of inappropriate behavior.

STUDENT RESEARCH AND INNOVATION PROGRAM Description One of the core commitments of the University of Cabuyao is to create, apply, and communicate research-based knowledge that is significant to industry and society.
At the heart of this commitment is a focus on prioritizing and emphasizing the importance of research in the educational experience of the student.
The University recognizes that research provides a unique opportunity for students to develop critical thinking, problem-solving, and analytical skills, while also fostering a deeper understanding of the subject matter.
To ensure that research conducted by students meets the highest standards of quality, the University measures the quality of research by several different criteria.
These criteria include the format of the research paper or project, the logical presentation of the research findings, the theoretical foundation upon which the research is based, the consistency and coherence of the research arguments, the quality of language development, and the credibility and reliability of the sources cited in the research.
By setting high standards for research quality, the University seeks to foster a culture of excellence in research among its students and faculty.
This not only benefits the institution but also contributes to the wider societal goal of advancing knowledge and innovation.
The University encourages and supports innovation and start-up projects among students, teaching, and non-teaching personnel of the University.
The guideline aims to create a conducive environment for the development of entrepreneurial skills and the commercialization of intellectual property.
The University intends to foster a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship among its students, teaching, and non-teaching personnel.

MESSAGE FROM THE CITY MAYOR/ CHAIRMAN OF THE BOARD Mahal naming mga mananaliksik, mga tagapayo, mga panel, at mga coordinator ng pananaliksik, Pinapaabot namin ang pinakamainit na pagbati at taos-pusong pasasalamat sa inyong mahahalagang kontribusyon sa larangan ng pananaliksik at pag-aaral.
Sa patuloy na pagbabago ng larangan ng akademya at pagtuklas, ang pananaliksik ay may malaking papel sa pagpapaunlad, paghubog ng mga patakaran, at pagharap sa mga hamon ng ating panahon.
Ang inyong kolektibong pagsisikap at intelektuwal na pagkilos ay may kakayahan na mag-anyo ng kinabukasan at transpormahin ang ating komunidad.
Sa pamamagitan ng mahigpit na mga metodolohiya, malawakang pagsusuri sa mga panitikan, at matalinong pagsusuri ng datos, inyong ibinibigay ang liwanag sa mga komplikadong isyu, nagpapakita ng mga bagong perspektibo, at nag-aambag sa pandaigdigang kaalaman.
Isa-isa, bilang isang kolektibong puwersa, ipinagdiriwang natin ang inyong paghahangad sa kaalaman, pagbabago, at intelektuwal na paglago.
Ang inyong pananaliksik ay nagiging tanglaw ng pag-asa, patungo sa mga solusyong batay sa ebidensya, nagtataguyod ng pangmatagalang kaunlaran, at nagpapayaman sa ating kolektibong pagkaunawa sa mundo na ating kinabibilangan.
Nawa'y maglingkod ang Student Research and Innovation Manual na ito bilang inyong pinagkakatiwalaang gabay, nag-aalok ng kaalaman, etikal na gabay, at mga pinakamahusay na pamamaraan na magtutulak sa inyo patungo sa inyong paglalakbay sa pananaliksik.
Sabay-sabay, ating itulak ang mga hangganan, lumikha ng kinabukasang itinayo sa kaalaman, pagbabago, at transformatibong pananaliksik.
HON.
DENNIS FELIPE C.
HAIN (Sgd) City Mayor/Chairman of the Board

MESSAGE FROM THE VICE PRESIDENT FOR PLANNING, RESEARCH, & EXTENSION Research is the cornerstone of our University's mission to generate knowledge, foster innovation, and address pressing societal challenges.
Through your unwavering commitment to research excellence, you become the catalysts of positive change and agents of transformative solutions.
To the student researchers, your inquisitive minds and tireless pursuit of answers fuel the engine of discovery, leading to new insights, breakthroughs, and innovative solutions that shape the world we live in.
To the student advisers, your expertise, wisdom, and commitment to nurturing young minds play a pivotal role in shaping the future generation of scholars and scientists.
To the esteemed panels and research coordinators, your commitment to maintaining the integrity of the research process is instrumental in elevating the quality and impact of our scholarly contributions.
May this Student Research and Innovation Manual serve as a guiding light, providing the necessary framework and ethical guidelines for conducting rigorous and impactful research.
Let it be a constant reminder of the immense responsibility we bear as knowledge seekers, and the potential we have to create positive change through our scholarly pursuits.
Let us unite in our commitment to push boundaries, foster innovation, and collaboratively contribute to the advancement and transformation of our academic community and society as a whole.
DR.
ZANDRA N.
MANINGAS (Sgd) Vice President, Planning, Research, and Extension

The university's team of experts has worked tirelessly to provide you with the most relevant and useful information to help you achieve your research goals.

At the University of Cabuyao, we foster a culture of innovation that transcends disciplines, encouraging curiosity, critical thinking, and problem-solving.
Embrace the mindset of innovation, challenge norms, and unleash your potential to create impactful solutions in your field of study.

• Embrace Collaboration: Engage in interdisciplinary projects, value diverse perspectives, and collaborate with peers.
• Embrace Failure: View failure as a stepping stone to success, learn from it, and use it to iterate and improve your ideas.
• Embrace Continuous Learning: Stay updated, explore new technologies, and have a lifelong commitment to learning.

As students of University of Cabuyao, you have a supportive academic community and abundant resources to fuel your innovation journey.
Engage in research, join competitions, and take advantage of our innovation-focused programs.
Embrace the culture of innovation, dream big, and become catalysts for positive change in your field.
We anticipate witnessing the remarkable contributions you will make as students of University of Cabuyao.
Let's embrace the spirit of innovation and together, create a brighter future.
Best regards!
ENGR.
CHERRY D.
CASUAT (Sgd) Director, Knowledge Management and Innovation Department

CHAPTER I STUDENT TERMINAL PROGRAM PNC:PRE-GU-21 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
Enrolling in Research is restricted to junior-senior standing students, as stated in their respective study programs.
2.
Non-graduating students may participate in research activities initiated by teaching or non-teaching personnel, involving alumni or industry partners.
3.
The Deans and Department Chairs oversee the Student Research Program and establish a timetable of activities before the start of the academic year to ensure that students meet the course requirements within a year.
The succeeding page provides the type of terminal research paper required for each degree program.

4.
The required type of research paper for each degree program is subject to change based on the recommendation of the Dean and in response to educational reforms and industry demands.
5.
Each type of research paper has its unique format and content requirements.
To ensure students are equipped with the necessary knowledge and skills, the Research Teacher provides lectures on all aspects of the research paper.
These lectures serve as the theoretical foundation that guides the students in developing their respective research papers.
6.

These presentations include the Title Conference, Proposal Defense, and Final Defense.
These oral presentations serve as opportunities for students to present their research findings, receive feedback, and demonstrate their understanding of the research topic.

7.
Following are the qualifications and roles and responsibilities of the key individuals involved in the research process a.
The Student-researcher shall: i.
Ensure the completion of the research project that has been agreed upon. ii.
Take the initiative to bring up any problems or difficulties you encounter during the research project to the appropriate parties, such as the Research Adviser and/or Research Teacher, for discussion and resolution. iii.
Be responsible for the direction, timeline, and progress of the research project, in coordination with the research adviser. iv.
Adhere to relevant rules, regulations, and ethical principles governing research, such as those related to the protection of human and animal subjects, confidentiality, data management, and conflicts of interest. v.
Ensure that the final research output is submitted within the prescribed period, taking into account the advice and recommendations of the Research Adviser and Research Teacher. vi.
Agree with the Research Adviser and/or Research Teacher on a schedule of regular meetings to discuss the progress of the research project and address any issues that arise. vii.
Submit research outputs for review and comment by the Research Adviser and Research Teacher at agreed-upon times to receive feedback and ensure that the research project is on track. b.
The Dean shall: i.
Review and approve both the proposed and final copy of the research paper submitted by the student-researcher. ii.
Recommending the Best Research Paper, which recognizes outstanding research projects that demonstrate excellence in research methodology, innovation, significance, and impact.

c.
The Department Chair shall: i.
Ensure the implementation of the research standards of the program, which includes providing guidance and support to student-researchers and ensuring that they comply with ethical and academic standards in conducting research. ii.
Be involved in the departmental screening committee for Best Research Paper Award, which involves reviewing and evaluating research projects to determine the winner of the award. d.
Research Teacher i.
Qualifications
• Preferably full-time faculty of the University
• With Master's degree of Thesis track or with research experience (evidenced by research outcomes or publications) in lieu of a thesis
• With at least "Satisfactory" rating based on previous evaluation (if applicable) ii.
Roles and Responsibilities
• Be responsible for supervising and monitoring the progress of the student-researcher, ensuring that they comply with the research format and adhere to the established timetable.
This involves providing guidance and feedback to help the student-researcher stay on track and make progress towards completing their research project.
• Collect and check the research output
• Collect and monitor the Thesis Advising Monitorng Form (PNC:PRE-FO-61)
• Collect assessment forms and analyze results PNC:PRE-FO-75 Thesis Adviser Evaluation Form PNC:PRE-FO-76 Panel Evaluation Form PNC:PRE-FO-77 Statistician Evaluation Form PNC:PRE-FO-83 Data Analyst Form (for qualitative research only)
• Assist the students on research-related problems and questions
• Compile a list of advisers and submit it to the Dean
before the Prelim exam for future reference.

• Verify that the topic aligns with the University's research agenda and avoid duplicating research topics.
• Monitor and assess the research progress by strictly adhering to the output timetable.
• Conduct lectures on research methodology and related topics.
• Calculate and record students' grades.
• Attend meetings organized by the Dean, Department Chair, or Research and Development Department related to student research.
• Manage the research proceedings during presentations.
• Provide close guidance to the students to ensure they are on track with their research writing.
• Ensure that the students have paid the research-related fees e.
Research Adviser i.
Qualifications
• Preferably full-time teaching personnel of the University.
Part-time teaching personnel may be given advisorship, as needed.
• The VPAA, RDD Director, Deans, and Department Chairs (directly under their jurisdiction) are not allowed to accept advisorship.
• With Master's degree of Thesis track or with research experience (evidenced by research outcomes or publications) in lieu of a thesis
• With at least "Very Satisfactory" evaluation rating (PNC:PRE-FO-75) based on previous advisees' evaluation.
If the adviser got a mean average rating of unsatisfactory, s/he will be suspended for a year in advising student research.
After the cleansing period of one year, s/he will be included again in the roster of Research Adviser.
• Possess and maintain knowledge of the research area to provide adequate supervision of the research project.
• Possess and continue to develop the appropriate skills to facilitate the production of high-quality research work by the student/s.

ii.
Roles and Responsibilities
• Determine the research topic's feasibility and ethical soundness.
• Oversee and ensure satisfactory progress and completion of the research project as agreed upon.
• Develop and provide an appropriate schedule for each stage of the research project to meet the deadline.
• Promote high research ethics standards for students, emphasizing the avoidance of misconduct such as plagiarism or data fabrication.
• Notify the student/s of unsatisfactory progress or work quality and take any necessary action to support them.
• Be available for regular contact with the student/s, providing adequate time to meet their individual research needs.
• Review the student's written work and provide constructive feedback.
• Maintain clear, accurate, detailed, and accessible records of the student's work.
• Arrange consultation hours for students to seek advice and guidance.
• Conduct mock defense prior to proposal and final defense
• Introduce advisees and address concerns before and after the defense.
• Attend the student's defense as an observer and take notes but not participate in the presentation.
• Communicate regularly with Research Teachers regarding the students' progress and status.
• Inform the student/s about the rules and regulations governing the collaborating organization's premises, working practices, health, safety, and confidentiality.
• Ensure that the research paper undergoes a language and plagiarism check using appropriate software. f.
Research Statistician/ Data Analyst (as needed) i.

ii.

• Evaluate and approve the research proposal and completed work.

10.
Any student researcher who violates the rules and regulations of the University during the conduct of their research may face sanctions or penalties. a.
Students who commit plagiarism, or the act of copying previous terminal papers without proper citation, will face penalties during the following instances: i.
Plagiarism during the proposal or final defense will result in a failing grade for the research course. ii.
Plagiarism during the Midterm and Final Term will result in a failing grade only for the particular term when the plagiarism is committed. b.
Students are prohibited from commissioning someone to prepare the research, including software for CCS and prototypes for Engineering, or they will receive a failing mark. c.
For other violations by the student-researchers not covered by this guideline, they must be reported to SASD for appropriate disciplinary actions and sanctions.
11.
Below is the computation of grade for Student Research.
For Midterm Standing: Assessment Task: Average of Requirements (Research Teacher) = 40 % Examination (Research Output/Concept Paper) = 60 % Total 100% For Final Standing: Assessment Task: Average of Requirements (Research Teacher) = 30 % Examination (Proposal/Final Defense Grade) = 70 % Total 100% 12.
The Final Rating is computed as follows: MIDTERM STANDING + FINAL STANDING = FINAL RATING (60%) (40%) (100%) 13.
All researches with human participants/respondents shall make use of the Informed Consent Form (PNC:PRE-FO-50) before the actual conduct of data gathering.
Its intent is that human participants can
enter research freely (voluntarily) with full information about what it means for them to take part, and that they give consent before they enter the research.

b.
The Research Teacher shall issue the Statistician/Data Analyst Commitment Form (PNC:PRE-FO-60) to be accomplished and signed by the selected statistician by the students. c.
Student-researcher has the right to change statistician/data analyst for a justifiable reason/s but subject to the approval of the Dean/Department Chair.
Student Research Adviser/ Statistician/Data Analyst Changing Form (PNC:PRE-FO-62) shall be accomplished by the concerned student-researcher. d.
Records of consultation shall be retained using the prescribed form (PNC:PRE-FO-81).
3.
On Student Research Groups a.
Students are allowed to choose their group mates provided that each group does not exceed three members for collegiate departments.
Student Research Grouping Form (PNC:PRE-FO-130) shall be accomplished by the concerned student-researcher. b.
For graduate school, a thesis shall be done individually. c.
If the topic is too complex, the group may be allowed to have less than 5 members as per recommendation of the Research Teacher prior to approval of the Dean. d.
Student-researcher has the right to change members for a justifiable reason/s but subject to the approval of the Dean/ Department Chair.
Student Research Re-grouping Form (PNC:PRE-FO-130) shall be accomplished by the concerned student-researcher. e.
Each group selects a leader to represent their group in any student research-related concerns (as need arises).
4.
On Title Approval a.
The student researchers submit to Research Adviser utmost three topics/titles using the PNC:PRE-FO-66 Proposed Student Research Topics for initial review. b.
The Research Teacher shall schedule Title Defense, where the recommended three topics shall be presented and evaluated
by the panelists.

PNC:PRE-FO-67 (Research Title Assessment Form) shall be utilized by the panelists. c.
The composition of the Research Committee is as follows i.
Two internal panel members ii.
Research Teacher iii.
Research Adviser.
S/he is not allowed to participate during the presentation.
His or her opinions may be shared during the deliberation, as needed d.
The following are the bases in approving the topic: i. they adhere to the institution's research agenda; ii. they are relevant to the current societal issues or technological trends iii. they clearly state the problem to be solved/compelling reasons of the study as evidence of stakeholder's consultation iv. they are ethically sound v. they are publishable vi. they follow the standard number of words used for research title typically 10-12 words long vii. they are aligned with the field of discipline of the researchers e.
Once approved, if the proposed topics/titles will be conducted in Pamantasan ng Cabuyao, the student researcher must accomplish and submit a notarized University's Confidentiality and Non-Disclosure Agreement for Research Student (PNC:PRE-FO-68) to ensure the protection of information between the researchers and University.
The form will be distributed to students through Research Teacher. f.
The Research Teacher shall submit to the Dean a summary of the student research groups and their approved titles using the Summary of Student Research (PNC:PRE-FO-69). g.
Student-researcher has the right to change topic for a justifiable reason/s but subject to the recommendation of the research teacher prior to the approval of the Dean.

5.
On Proposal Defense a.
The Research Teacher sets the schedule of the defense.
All groups must defend their research proposals on the scheduled dates. b.
Prior to the Proposal defense, the student-researchers shall submit the following requirements to the Research Teacher. i.
Soft copy of the completed and edited research proposal ii.
Full report of plagiarism and language softwares iii.
Duly accomplished and signed Recommendation Form (PNC:PRE-FO-71) iv.
Confidentiality and Non-Disclosure Agreement for Student Research (for researches conducted in Pamantasan ng Cabuyao) (PNC:PRE-FO-68) v.
Thesis Advising and Commitment Form (PNC:PRE-FO-61) vi.
Official receipt of Proposal Defense Fee, Adviser's Fee, Editor's Fee, and Payment for Student Handbook. vii.
Photocopy of PNC:PRE-FO-67 (Research Title Assessment Form) as proof that the proposed topic was approved. viii.
Research Ethics Application Form (PNC:PRE-FO-49) c.
The Research Teacher shall inform the panelists of the schedule and venue of defense or online credentials and forwards the schedule to the Department Chair for reference purposes. d.
The group that fails to submit their research proposal on the designated date, is given another chance within a week upon presentation of valid reasons through formal letter noted by the Research Teacher and approved by the Dean.
However, a 1% deduction each day the proposal is late (excluding Saturdays, Sundays, or Holidays) shall be taken from the student's grade. e.
The composition of the Research Committee is as follows: i.
Two internal panel members ii.
Research Teacher iii.
Research Adviser.
S/he is not allowed to participate during the presentation.

They must critique and write their comments/suggestions on the Panel Comment Sheet (PNC:PRE-FO-72) provided by the Research Teacher.
Only those comments in the comment sheet shall be entertained by the student-researchers. g.
The Research Teacher shall moderate the deliberation of critical issues or questions. h.
Student-presenters are expected to be in their business/ corporate attire during the paper presentation. i.
For in-person defense, all the visual equipment and materials needed in the presentation must be arranged and prepared by the Research Teacher.
For virtual presentation, the online credentials shall be prepared and communicated by the Research Teacher. j.
Students are not allowed to provide food, token, or any form of gifts for their Research Committee during the proposal defense. k.
In case the defense schedule conflicts with the students' class schedule, they shall prepare an excuse letter noted by the respective Research Teacher and forward to concerned class teachers. l.
The student-presenters must come on time.
Late comers will not be accommodated in the presentation, thus, will be re-scheduled with a re-defense status. m.
Each group is given an hour to present the proposal.
The time schedule is divided into three parts: Presentation 15 minutes Question and Answer 40 minutes Deliberation 5 minutes n.
During deliberation, the Proposal Defense Evaluation Form (PNC:PRE-FO-73) must be accomplished (immediately after the presentation of each group) and submitted to the Research Teacher.

8.
On Selection of Best Research a.
The Dean shall submit the top three research groups to the VPAA.
The selection of candidates shall be based on the Final Oral Defense group grade.
All groups whose group grade is 90.00% or above with no panelist's group grade lower than 85.00% are considered candidates. b.
Candidates must submit the terminal requirements on time, otherwise, the group will be disqualified in the evaluation for Best Research Paper Award. c.
The top three groups of each degree program will undergo final deliberation by the Academic Council. d.
The Academic Council shall select the Best Research for each program. e.
The basis of evaluation are as follows: FOR CCS and COE PARAMETERS % Originality/Innovativeness 20% Relevance of the study to any of the following categories:
• Development of CALABARZON 10%
• Requirements of accreditation and certifying bodies
• Priorities of the City Government of Cabuyao
• PnC Philosophy and Objectives
• PnC Research Agenda Accuracy of Data and Facts Presented 10% Appropriateness of Methodology Used 10% Consistency and Validity of Findings, Conclusions, and Recommendations 10% Clarity and Formality of Language Used, Grammar and Syntax, Adherence to Prescribed Formatting Guide 5% Usability, Functionality, Reliability, and Completeness of the Software and Prototype 25% Extent of Literature Cited 10%
For other programs PARAMETERS % Originality/Innovativeness 20% Relevance of the study to any of the following categories:
• Development of CALABARZON 10%
• Requirements of accreditation and certifying bodies
• Priorities of the City Government of Cabuyao
• PnC Philosophy and Objectives

10.
Patent Search for Engineering.
Performing a patent research on student researches involves searching for existing patents or published patent applications related to the students' research topics.
By following the following steps, the students can gain valuable insights into the existing patent landscape related to their research and make informed decisions about the patentability and commercialization potential of their inventions. a.
Define the Research Topic: Clearly identify the specific research topic or invention concept that the student is working on.
Understand the unique features and technical aspects of the project to use relevant keywords during the search. b.
Keyword Search: Conduct a keyword search using online patent databases and search engines.
Use specific and relevant keywords related to the research topic to narrow down the search results. c.
Use Patent Classification: Utilize patent classification systems such as the International Patent Classification (IPC) or Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC) to categorize and filter patents related to the research area. d.
Prior Art Search: Look for prior art, which includes existing patents, published patent applications, and other publicly available technical documents relevant to the research topic.
Prior art helps determine the novelty and non-obviousness of the student's invention. e.
Search Multiple Databases: Utilize various patent databases and search engines, such as the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO), European Patent Office (EPO), World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), and Google Patents, to ensure comprehensive coverage of relevant patents. f.

Analyze Patent Documents: Carefully review the patent documents found during the search.
Pay close attention to the patent claims, which define the scope of protection granted to the invention.
Compare the students' research with the patented inventions to assess the novelty and potential patentability.

Note Similarities and Differences: Identify any patents that are closely related to the students' research and note the similarities and differences between their work and the patented inventions.
This will help the students understand the existing technology landscape and potential areas for improvement or differentiation. h.
Seek Legal Assistance: If the students' research shows potential for patentability, it is advisable to seek advice from the Director for Knowledge Management and Innovation Department.
S/he can help determine whether the invention meets the patentability criteria and guide the students through the patent application process. i.

This documentation will be valuable for future reference and to demonstrate due diligence in conducting the patent research.

Research should be written in clear and concise language that is accessible to a wide audience.

The summary shows the history, highlights, descriptive definitions, long-range objectives, feasibility criteria for FS, and main conclusions of the project under study. ii.

CHAPTER II INSTITUTIONAL AND STUDENT RESEARCH ETHICS REVIEW PNC:PRE-GU-13 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
It is the responsibility of all researchers to adhere to the principles and procedures outlined in this guideline to ensure that research activities are conducted in an ethical and responsible manner.
2.
All research proposals involving humans as participants/subjects shall be submitted to RERC for ethics review and clearance.
This follows various international and national guidelines that have been developed for the protection of human participants in research.
3.
All researchers must include a description that outlines the ethical considerations of their studies in protocols/methodologies.
4.
Research Ethics Review Committee (RERC) a.
The committee shall govern the ethics of research across the University.
It ensures the dignity, protection of rights, health and safety and privacy of human subjects, the welfare of animals, and the integrity of the environment.
It also upholds the academic freedom, health, and safety of researchers and the reputation of the University as an institution of high-quality research. b.
The RERC comprises seven members with various educational backgrounds.
A legal representative shall be invited to serve as a regular member of the committee.
Further, an independent consultant shall be invited to guide the RERC, as needed.

c.
The scope of work of the RERC covers all researches involving human participants for completion of an undergraduate thesis, graduate research, faculty researches as well as researches referred by other institutions such as HEIs, government agencies, among others. d.
The creation of the Research Ethics Review Committee (RERC) is in compliance with the guidelines set forth by the Philippine National Health Research System (PNHRS), specifically the Philippine Health Research Ethics Board (PHREB); the DOST, DOH, CHED, UPM Joint Memorandum Order 2012-001, which outlines the requirements for ethical review of health research involving human participants; and the DOST-PCHRD, DOH, CHED, UPM-NIH Administrative Order 001-2013, which serves as the implementing rules and regulations of RA 10532, or the Philippine National Health Research System Act of 2013. e.
In accordance with the University's commitment to upholding the highest ethical standards in research, the RERC operates independently of other offices, units, and administrative officials in the university.
This independence is essential to ensuring that the review and decision-making process of the RERC is objective, impartial, and free from any external influence. f.
Therefore, the decisions of the RERC with respect to its reviews of research protocols are not subject to the influence, regulation, or approval of any other office or official in the institution.
The RERC operates with complete autonomy and makes decisions based solely on the merits of the research proposals that come before it, without any undue influence from external sources. g.

It also helps to maintain the integrity of the research enterprise and promotes public trust in the University and its research activities.

Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
All research proposals must be submitted for research ethics review prior to the start of the research project.
The research ethics review process must ensure that the research proposal adheres to the principles outlined in this policy framework.
2.
All researchers should adhere to the following principles: a.
Respect for Human Dignity.
All research activities must respect all human beings' inherent dignity and worth. b.
Informed Consent.
Informed consent (PNC:PRE-FO-50) must be obtained from all research participants before conducting any research activities.
All research participants must be provided with clear and understandable information about the research project, including any potential risks and benefits associated with participation.
Informed consent must be obtained from all research participants prior to their participation in the research project.
Parental consent form (PNC:PRE-FO-51) shall be accomplished for research participants who are below 18 years old. c.
Privacy and Confidentiality.
All research activities must respect the privacy and confidentiality of research participants.
Researchers must take all necessary steps to protect the privacy and confidentiality of research participants. d.
Responsibility for Safety.
All researchers have a responsibility to ensure that the research activities are conducted safely and responsibly.

e.
Integrity and Accountability.
All research activities must be conducted with the highest levels of integrity and accountability.
Researchers must ensure that the research is conducted in a transparent and responsible manner, and that all data collected is accurate and verifiable.
3.
Confidentiality Agreement Form (PNC:PRE-FO-47) and Disclosure of Conflict of Interest Form PNC:PRE-FO-48) a.
The members of the RERC play a crucial role in ensuring that research studies conducted at the institution are ethical and comply with all relevant guidelines and regulations.
To ensure the integrity of the review process, it is essential that all members of the RERC maintain strict confidentiality and disclose any potential conflicts of interest. b.
To this end, all members of the RERC are required to sign a Confidentiality Agreement Form (PNC:PRE-FO-47) and a Disclosure of Conflict of Interest Form (PNC:PRE-FO-48). c.
The Confidentiality Agreement Form outlines the obligations of RERC members to maintain strict confidentiality with respect to all research proposals and related documents that come before the committee.
This includes not disclosing any information related to the proposals to any unauthorized third party or using such information for personal gain or advantage. d.
The Disclosure of Conflict of Interest Form requires all RERC members to disclose any potential conflicts of interest that could impact their ability to review research proposals objectively and impartially.
This includes financial interests, personal relationships, or any other factors that could influence their decision-making. e.

By signing these forms, RERC members acknowledge their commitment to upholding the highest ethical standards in the review of research proposals and their willingness to disclose any potential conflicts of interest that could compromise the integrity of the review process.
This helps to ensure that the
review process is fair, transparent, and free from bias, and ultimately helps to protect the rights and welfare of research participants.
4.
Research Ethics Review a.
Exempted Review i.
Research projects that involve the collection of data from publicly available databases or public documents are exempt from review. ii.
This exemption recognizes that the collection of data from public sources is generally considered to pose minimal risk to research participants, and as such, does not require the same level of review and scrutiny as other research activities. b.
Expedited Review i.
Expedited Review is used for research proposals that are deemed to have lower complexity and minimal risk.
These are typically studies that involve standard research procedures and pose minimal harm to participants. ii.
Expedited review shall be conducted for the following:
• Research projects that pose minimal risk to participants and involve standard, non-invasive procedures are prime candidates for expedited review.
These studies do not expose participants to risks greater than what they might encounter in their daily lives or routine medical check-ups.
• Research that consists of anonymous or de-identified surveys, questionnaires, or interviews may qualify for expedited review, especially when the questions are not sensitive in nature and the risks are minimal.

Research Ethics Application Form (PNC:PRE-FO-49) a.
All research proposals that involve human participants/subjects be submitted to our RERC for ethics review and clearance.
This requirement applies to all research activities conducted within our institution, regardless of funding source or affiliation. b.
By subjecting all research proposals involving human participants/subjects to ethics review and clearance, the University ensures that the rights, welfare, and dignity of research participants are protected, and that research activities are conducted in a responsible and ethical manner.
This also helps to ensure that the University complies with relevant laws, regulations, and ethical standards governing research involving human participants/subjects. c.
The Research Ethics Application Form shall be processed by the RERC. d.
Results of the RERC Review (PNC:PRE-FO-52) shall be sent via email to the concerned researcher. e.
For researches with minor revisions, the researcher(s) must address the Committee's concerns and resubmit the revised materials for final approval. f.
For researches with major revisions, The researchers must address the Committee's concerns and resubmit the revised materials for a second round of review.

Management of RERC Post-Approval Submissions (PNC:PRE-FO-95).
This should be submitted to the RERC online, together with the final requirements on final manuscripts.

a.
Final Manusripts i.
Submission Timeline: Researchers are required to submit Final Manuscripts to their research teachers upon completion of the research project or at the end of the approved study period. ii.
Content: Final manuscript should provide a comprehensive summary of the research, including results, data analysis, conclusions, and any ethical considerations.
Any protocol deviations, SAEs, or unanticipated issues should also be included. iii.
Review Process: Final Reports undergo a thorough review to verify that the research was conducted in adherence to the approved protocol and that ethical standards were upheld throughout the study. b.
Early Termination Reports i.
Submission Timeline: Researchers must promptly submit an Early Termination Report, using the prescribed form, if the research is terminated prematurely for any reason. ii.
Content: Early Termination Reports should explain the reasons for the premature termination and provide any relevant information about participant safety and data integrity. iii.
Review Process: The RERC reviews Early Termination Reports to assess the reasons for termination and to ensure that appropriate steps were taken to protect participants and data. c.
Protocol Amendments i.
Submission Timeline: Researchers must submit protocol amendments, using the prescribed form, for any proposed changes to the approved research protocol before
implementing the changes. ii.
Content: Protocol Amendments should include a detailed description of the proposed changes, rationale, potential implications for participant safety, and any updated informed consent documents. iii.

Review Process: Protocol Amendments are reviewed by the RERC to determine whether the proposed changes are ethically sound and whether participant safety is adequately addressed. d.
Review of SAE & SUSAR Reports for Psychology and Nursing researches i.
Submission Timeline: Researchers are required to promptly report any Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) and Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions (SUSARs) , using the prescribed form, as they occur during the research. ii.
Content: SAE & SUSAR Reports should include a detailed description of the event, its potential relationship to the research, actions taken, and the impact on participant safety. iii.
Review Process: SAE & SUSAR Reports are promptly reviewed to assess participant safety and ensure that appropriate actions were taken. e.
Review of Protocol Deviations & Violations i.
Submission Timeline: Researchers must report protocol deviations or violations, using the prescribed form, as they occur during the research. ii.
Content: Reports should describe the nature of the deviation or violation, the circumstances surrounding it, actions taken to mitigate risks, and steps to prevent recurrence.

iii.
Review Process: Deviations and violations are reviewed to assess their impact on participant safety and data integrity.
The RERC ensures that corrective actions are taken.
7.
Management of Queries and Complaints a.
The RERC recognizes the importance of addressing queries and complaints effectively to uphold ethical research practices and maintain transparency. b.
Formal queries and complaints shall be sent via email (rdd@ pnc.edu.ph).
The confidentiality of the individuals shall be handled with the utmost confidentiality to encourage open communication. c.
The RDD Director shall be responsible for initial assessments.
S/he shall ensure that all queries and complaints receive an initial response acknowledging receipt within a reasonable timeframe, typically within five business days. d.
The RDD Director shall ensure that a resolution has been reached to address the concerns raised in the query or complaint.
This may involve implementing corrective actions, making policy adjustments, or providing additional information. e.
The complainant shall be notify of the investigation's findings and any actions taken to address their concerns. f.
RERC shall utilize feedback from queries and complaints to improve RERC guidelines and forms.
8.
RERC Meetings. a.
Meetings should be scheduled at regular intervals as per the established timeline.
The schedule should be communicated to all RERC members well in advance. b.
The RERC Chair, in consultation with the committee, should create an agenda that outlines the order of business for the
meeting.

The agenda should include standard items such as call to order, approval of minutes, new research proposals, protocol amendments, progress reports, and any other relevant items. c.
The RERC Chair shall ensure that all research proposals and related materials are received well in advance to allow members adequate time for review. d.
In preparation for the meeting, the RERC Secretary or designated member should collect all relevant documents, including research proposals, amendments, progress reports, and any other relevant materials. e.
Members are expected to thoroughly review the research proposals and supporting documentation before the meeting to ensure meaningful discussions. f.
Members should uphold strict confidentiality regarding the content of the research proposals and discussions during the meeting. g.
The RERC Chair shall Ensure that a quorum is met to conduct official business. h.
The RERC Chair shall assign time limits to each agenda item to ensure efficient use of meeting time. i.
On Conduct of Regular and Special Meetings. i.
Regular Meetings
• Call to Order: The Chair calls the meeting to order at the scheduled time.
• Approval of Minutes: Members review and approve the minutes from the previous meeting.
• New Research Proposals: Discuss and review new research proposals, ensuring they comply with ethical standards and regulations.
• Protocol Amendments: Review and discuss any
proposed protocol amendments, taking into consideration their impact on participant safety and research integrity.
• Discussion and Decision: Engage in in-depth discussions on each agenda item, seeking clarification and addressing concerns.

CHAPTER III RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS AND SERVICES PNC:PRE-GU-15 Section 1.
General Policies The Research and Development Department (RDD) serves as the primary research arm of the University, tasked with promoting and sustaining a culture of research among the faculty and students.
Through its research programs and services, the RDD aims to support the institution's thrust in conducting research studies that contribute to advancing knowledge and improving the local community.
Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
Research Colloquium. a.
Output of all researches conducted under Institutional Research Program must be disseminated through a research colloquium. b.
All research colloquium scheduled by RDD is open to all interested personnel and students of the University. c.
The RDD formally informs the researcher of the schedule of the research colloquium through a letter. d.
Guidelines for paper presentation will be provided by RDD. e.
Open forum will ensue after the presentation of the research outcomes. f.
RDD and Program Chair/Dean shall invite three evaluators for institutional and research colloquium.
They may invite one external evaluator who is a reputable expert or a practitioner
in the field.
The evaluation ensues based on the procedure and criteria set by the RDD.
2.
Research Capability Building Activities a.
The RDD organizes trainings, workshops, and seminars for all University personnel.
The ultimate goal of these activities is to develop their research capability, which would eventually lead to a sustainable research culture within the University. b.

To ensure the training meets the needs of the target participants, the RDC conducts a thorough assessment of training needs. c.
The RDD organizes specialized research trainings that are tailored to the participants' field of specialization.
Expert speakers or resource persons who possess in-depth knowledge or extensive experience on the topic are invited. d.
The frequency of research trainings, workshops, and seminars is determined based on the target(s) specified in the Department's strategic plan. e.
The research trainings, workshops, and seminars organized by RDD align with the Institutional Research Agenda of the University, ensuring their relevance and contribution to the overall research direction of the institution.
3.
Research Journal Publications a.
The University, through the Research and Development Center (RDD), provides avenues for PnC teaching and non-teaching personnel to share research outcomes to the general public through publications. b.
These academic journals contain pertinent research information on completed research studies conducted by Pamantasan ng Cabuyao teaching and non-teaching personnel and students evaluated as exemplary, within the research
priorities of the institution, and have not yet been printed in other journals or publications.
4.
Instructional Materials Development a.
The RDC serves as the screening house of unpublished instructional materials developed by University personnel, intended for University's adoption. b.
All research outcomes must undergo plagiarism check.
RDD sets the acceptable rating to 15% similarity based on the institutional plagiarism software report.

The Knowledge Management and Innovation Department monitors the actual usage of the recommendations of the research report, institutionally-funded, prototype, or software within and outside of the University.
Usage could be in the form of theory, practice, policy, or social action. b.

It refers to the mass production of University's research prototypes and software, and mass production of instructional materials.
It is a form of knowledge or technology transfer.

CHAPTER IV MANAGEMENT OF JOURNAL PUBLICATION PNC:PRE-GU-16 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
An Editorial Board shall be created by the University to maintain the integrity and quality of the journal, as well as ensuring that it meets the needs and interests of its readers and contributors.
2.
The RDD has publications titled: a.
PnC Dangal Research Refereed Journal
• Pamantasan ng Cabuyao Dangal Research Journal: Advancing Knowledge Scholarship Output b.
PnC Compendium of Institutional Research Abstracts
• Innovation & Insights: Institutional Creative and Impactful Research Studies c.
PnC Compendium of Student Research Abstracts
• Fresh Perspectives: Celebrating the Intellectual Curiosity of our Future Leaders d.
PnC Student Research Journal for Best Research Papers
• Pioneering Minds: Recognizing Excellence and Innovation in Student Scholarship Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
The RDD issues a call for paper.
Articles should be in every April 15 of the current year to facilitate editing and presswork.
The deadline may be extended by the RDD Director if the need arises.
2.
All completed researches under the Institutional Research Program shall be published in the PnC Dangal ng Bayan Research Journal.

This will be communicated to all researchers who intend to submit for publication.
4.
The journal will be final checked by the RDD Director and the VPPRE prior to publication.
5.
The journal cannot be reproduced, in part or whole, without permission from the publisher.
Requests to reprint the journal or any of its parts should be addressed to the RDD Director.
6.
The accuracy and veracity of articles are solely attributed to the authors.

8.
Editorial Board a.
Selection i.
The editorial board will be selected by the Research and Development Department and shall be recommended for approval by the Vice President for Planning, Research, and Extension to the University President. ii.
Selection shall be based on their expertise in the journal's subject matter, their standing in the academic community, and their availability to fulfill the responsibilities of the position. iii.
The editorial board should be composed of individuals from diverse backgrounds and affiliations to ensure that the journal is representative of the larger academic community. b.

Journal Development

• Attend and participate in editorial board meetings
• Provide advice or feedback on matters pertaining to the development of the journal, including its editorial scope and focus, the appointment of new Editorial Board members, important conferences and promotional opportunities, market insights

Participate in peer review
• Review papers as instructed by the Editor-in-Chief using the prescribed form (PNC:PRE-FO-43)
• When discussing the manuscripts and the peer-review process, act impartially and with confidentially;
• Provide expert advice on whether the work could be approved for publication in the journal.
• Ensure the integrity of the peer-review process.
• Disclose conflicts of interest and recusing themselves from decisions related to manuscripts in which they have a conflict of interest. c.

Members of the editorial board will serve for a term of one year, which may be renewable at the discretion of the University President. d.
Removal: Members of the editorial board may be removed for cause, including, but not limited to, failure to fulfill their responsibilities, misconduct, or conflicts of interest that cannot be managed or resolved. e.
Confidentiality.

Conflicts of interest include, but are not limited to, financial interests, professional relationships, and personal relationships that may bias their
decisions.
The editor-in-chief will manage or resolve conflicts of interest as appropriate. g.

9.
Peer Review Process a.
All submitted manuscripts will be subjected to a rigorous peer-review process.
The review process will be anonymous and conducted by experts in the field. b.
The peer-review process shall be double-blind, where the identities of the authors and reviewers are kept confidential. c.
The peer reviewers will provide feedback and recommendations to the editorial board regarding the manuscript's quality and suitability for publication. d.
Reviewers shall provide feedback on the research article, including its strengths, weaknesses, and any areas for improvement. e.
The editorial board shall make a decision based on the feedback received from the reviewers.

Publication Frequency a.
The journal will be published on once a year. b.
The publication schedule will be communicated to potential authors and subscribers.
11.
Publication Standards. a.
All published articles will be of high quality and adhere to the standards set forth by the journal.

Marketing and Promotion a.

CHAPTER V INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS PNC:PRE-GU-18 Section 1.
General Policies 1.
The Knowledge Management and Innovation Department (KMID) shall be the coordinating office of the University with Intellectual Property Office of the Philippines (IPO-PHL) on applying for intellectual property-related matters of institutional and student researches in the University 2.
KMID shall spearhead the promotion of utilization and technology transfer of research outcomes within the University and to prospective industry companies.
3.
The University shall own the intellectual property rights created by teaching and non-teaching personnel as part of his/her duties and those created by students under the conditions stated in the succeeding section.
4.
Research outcomes with potential intellectual property value presented in public either by colloquium, symposium, conference, or exhibit shall only be given 10 months to apply for the outcome for protection with IPO-PHL from the date of presentation.
Otherwise, these will lose their novelty and will no longer qualify for registration.
Section 2.
Specific Policies 1.
On IP Creation a.
Innovation is embedded in the University's mission, and it is dedicated to fostering a culture of creativity.
With the implementation of InnovateUC, the University aims to elevate academic experiences and propel the institution into a
hub of groundbreaking ideas.
Recognizing the importance of intellectual property, the University will encourage the creation, protection, and commercialization of novel concepts. b.

passages.title: UC-PnC Student Research and Innovation Manual

passages.text:
GUIDELINES > CHAPTER V INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS > Section 2. Specific Policies
The KMID shall secure intellectual property protection to facilitate the commercialization of works, trademarks, innovations, inventions, and safeguard scientifically significant discoveries. c.
Performing patent research on institutional and student researches involves searching for existing patents or published patent applications related to the research topics (cf: PnC: PRE-GU-12 Institutional Research Program and PnC:PRE-GU-21 Student Terminal Project). d.
In line with UC PnC commitment to promoting a culture of transparency, collaboration, and responsible intellectual property management, all IP Creators are required to disclose their developments to the University, using the prescribed form (PnC:PRE-FO-99). e. f.
Within one month of receiving the IP Disclosure form, KMID shall communicate in writing to the IP creator, confirming whether the University intends to pursue the registration and/ or commercialization of the IP, taking into consideration any obligations to external parties. g.
The IP creator is obligated to maintain the confidentiality of technology details while the University assesses the feasibility of commercialization and/or registration.
Any form of publication, including verbal disclosure, describing a plant, invention, innovation, or discovery before patent filing could jeopardize the registration process. h.
Throughout the evaluation, the IP creator must refrain from public disclosure until the appropriate IP application has been filed.
University is committed to minimizing delays in the application process.

i.
The IP creator is required to promptly disclose to the University the identity of any party expressing interest in commercially exploiting the IP, providing sufficient detail as soon as relevant facts become known. j.
IP creators must disclose any conflicts of interest to the University, ensuring transparency in their engagement with the intellectual property.
They shall submit a duly signed Disclosure of Conflict of Interest Form (PNC:PRE-FO-48) and Confidentiality Agreement Form (PNC:PRE-FO-47).
2.
On Research Contracts a.
The University President, through the Vice President for Planning, Research, and Extension, shall engage in research contracts, including commissioned research, collaborative research, or sponsored research.
These agreements may involve financial support from government institutions, private funding bodies, whether local or international, or private industries or companies. b.
The University shall own the intellectual property rights created by teaching and non-teaching personnel as part of his/ her duties and those created by students under the conditions stated in the succeeding pages. c.
The specific items to be included in such contracts can vary depending on the nature of the intellectual property and the agreement between the university and relevant parties.
However, following are key elements that should be observed in research contracts: i.
Definition of Intellectual Property: Clearly define what constitutes intellectual property under the contract, encompassing inventions, patents, copyrights, trademarks, trade secrets, and any other relevant creations. ii.

Ownership of Intellectual Property: Specify the ownership of intellectual property rights, outlining whether the university, the IP Creator, or both parties share ownership.

This includes distinctions between foreground and background intellectual property. iii.
Creator's Rights and Obligations: Detail the rights and obligations of the creator(s) of the intellectual property, including disclosure requirements, confidentiality obligations, and the responsibility to cooperate in the protection and commercialization process. iv.
Commercialization and Licensing: Clearly state the terms and conditions for commercializing the intellectual property, including licensing agreements.
Specify whether the university or the creator has the right to commercialize, and if applicable, the revenue-sharing arrangements. v.
Use and Access Rights: Outline any use or access rights granted to the university, collaborators, or third parties, ensuring clarity on the scope and limitations of such rights. vi.
Publication and Public Disclosure: Address the timing and conditions for publication and public disclosure of the intellectual property to avoid jeopardizing potential patent applications. vii.
Confidentiality and Non-Disclosure: Include provisions on confidentiality to protect sensitive information related to the intellectual property, especially during the early stages of development. viii.
Dispute Resolution: Establish mechanisms for resolving disputes that may arise during the course of the contract, including provisions for mediation, arbitration, or legal action. ix.
Indemnification: Specify indemnification clauses to protect both parties from legal liabilities arising from the use or commercialization of the intellectual property. x.

Term and Termination: Define the duration of the agreement and the conditions under which it can be terminated, including any rights and obligations post-termination. xi.
Governing Law and Jurisdiction: Specify the governing law and jurisdiction under which the contract will be interpreted and enforced. xii.
Ethical Considerations: Address any ethical considerations related to the use and application of the intellectual
property, particularly in fields such as biotechnology or sensitive research areas. xiii.
Compliance with University Policies: Ensure that the contract aligns with the university's policies and guidelines regarding intellectual property, research, and technology transfer. xiv.
Assignment of Rights: Detail any provisions related to the assignment or transfer of intellectual property rights to third parties. xv.
KMID Involvement: Clearly define the role of the university's KMID in managing and overseeing intellectual property matters 3.
On Ownership of IP and Rights of Use a.
Intellectual Property Rights This will cover patents, industrial design, Utility Models, and among others. i.
The University shall own the patents and the right to register the IPs of creations/inventions/outcomes produced in the University that fall under the following qualifications:
• Creations/outcomes/inventions are fully funded by the University
• Creations/outcomes/inventions are part of the creator/ inventor/IP Creator's regular duties and responsibilities.
• Developed creations/outcomes/inventions that used the University's facilities, equipment, and resources.
• Creations/outcomes/inventions are assigned in writing by the inventor to the University.

• Commissioned work by Pamantasan ng Cabuyao.
• In the case of students, the invention or work was developed when he/she received financial support from PnC in the form of tuition, scholarship, stipend, or allowance regardless of the amount.
• Works whose inventors cannot be determined.

ii.
If the IP Creator violates any provisions in the agreement with the University, or any institutional guideline relating to the outcome, the University shall be the sole owner of the patent. iii.
For research outcomes/inventions that are sourced by the University, wholly or partially, from external entities, RDD shall negotiate with the funding organization with respect to the ownership of copyright or patent rights and royalty sharing.
In the absence of a negotiated agreement, all patents or inventions and copyrights of research outcomes shall be owned by the University. iv.
Reversion of ownership.
• In the event that PnC decides not to file a patent application or claim ownership of the patent within one hundred (100) days from the initial discussion of the said invention with the management, ownership of the invention or the work shall automatically revert to the IP Creator subject to the agreement, if any, entered into by PnC with a funding or sponsoring agency prior to the research.
• If it is established that the IP holds no commercial or strategic value, the University shall consider initiating the reversion process.
• If the student expresses the intention to apply for patent or copyright independently, outside the scope of the best research program, discuss the implications of such a decision and assess whether reversion of ownership is appropriate.I
• If the university has held ownership of an IP for a specified period, and efforts to commercialize or monetize the IP have been unsuccessful, there may be provisions in agreements allowing for the reversion of ownership to the original creator.

• In some cases, if the original creator requests the reversion of ownership and is willing to comply with certain conditions or repay any invested resources by the university, the institution may consider such
requests.
• If the creator of the IP leaves the university, and the IP is not directly related to ongoing university projects or research, there may be considerations for reversion of ownership, especially if the creator desires to continue development independently.
• If the university fails to fulfill its obligations as outlined in the IP agreement, and this failure negatively impacts the commercialization or development of the IP, the agreement might stipulate reversion as a remedy. b.
Ownership of Trademark.
PnC exclusively owns the trademarks, service marks, emblems, logos, symbols and other marks that it uses and distributes in relation to its goods or services.
The KMID shall be responsible for the registration and management of all marks of PnC.
The RDD and the KMID have the authority to engage in or approve the development and design of the registered marks of PnC.
4.
Publication, Non-Disclosure, and Trade Secrets of Intellectual Property at the University of Cabuyao a.
Publication Guidelines: i.
Premature Publication.
IP Creators must exercise caution to avoid premature publication of intellectual property (IP) details.
The university emphasizes that public disclosure, whether through written or verbal means, should not occur before appropriate protection mechanisms are in place. ii.
Enabling Disclosure.
While promoting knowledge dissemination, IP Creators are encouraged to make enabling disclosures that contribute positively to the academic and scientific community.

passages.title: UC-PnC Student Research and Innovation Manual
passages.source: University LMS / UC-PnC Student Research and Innovation Manual
passages.page_or_section: GUIDELINES > CHAPTER V INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS > Section 2. Specific Policies (pp. 100-101)
passages.text:
GUIDELINES > CHAPTER V INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS > Section 2. Specific Policies
However, they should judiciously balance the need for sharing knowledge with protecting potential IP. iii.
Preventing Prejudicial Disclosure.
IP Creators should be vigilant to prevent prejudicial disclosure that could harm
the interests of the University of Cabuyao or compromise the novelty and protectability of IP.
This includes avoiding disclosures that might negatively impact patentability or other forms of protection. b.
Non-Disclosure Guidelines: i.
Confidential Information.
All parties involved in intellectual property-related activities must treat confidential information with the utmost care.
This includes safeguarding research findings, trade secrets, and any sensitive information integral to the innovation process. ii.
Obligation of Non-Disclosure.
Individuals privy to confidential information are legally obligated not to disclose such information to unauthorized parties.
Non-disclosure agreements may be implemented as necessary to formalize this commitment. iii.
Limited Disclosure for Collaboration.
Limited disclosure of confidential information may occur in collaborative endeavors.
However, it should be governed by formal agreements that outline the extent, purpose, and duration of such disclosures. c.
Trade Secrets Guidelines: i.
Identification of Trade Secrets.
The University of Cabuyao encourages the identification and documentation of trade secrets within the institution.
This includes confidential formulas, processes, techniques, or information providing a competitive advantage. ii.
Protection Mechanisms.
Robust protection mechanisms should be implemented to safeguard trade secrets, including restricted access, encryption, and contractual agreements.

iii.
Limited Access.
Access to trade secrets should be limited to individuals with a legitimate need for such information.
Proper authorization processes should be in place to control access. iv.
Non-Compete and Non-Disclosure Agreements.
Individuals privy to trade secrets may be required to sign non-compete and non-disclosure agreements, reinforcing the legal protection of sensitive information. v.
Continual Monitoring and Evaluation.
The University of Cabuyao commits to continual monitoring and evaluation of trade secrets to ensure their continued relevance and protection.
Regular assessments will be conducted to update security measures as needed.
5.
Commercialization of Intellectual Property and Incentives a.
To facilitate the transfer of knowledge and technology of research outcomes, the IP Creators, in all applicable instances, shall grant to the University an exclusive worldwide license to reproduce, publish, publicly distribute copies, and apply for copyright or patent of the research outcomes. b.
The University shall explore opportunities to commercialize its intellectual property to maximize its value and impact. c.
The University shall undertake due diligence to identify potential commercial partners and assess the market potential of its intellectual property. d.
The University shall negotiate fair and reasonable terms in any licensing or commercialization agreements and ensure that such agreements are consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and contractual obligations. e.
In negotiating with the industry organizations that might take interest in commercializing the research outcomes, the industry shall sign a Confidentiality Agreement (PNC:PRE-
FO-47) and Non-Disclosure Agreement (PNC:PRE-FO-54).

The agreement serves as protection for the Pamantasan ng Cabuyao and the research proponents about any confidential information that will be divulged to the industry organization. f.
For University-funded research outcomes that are applied for commercialization, the royalty sharing shall be 60% for the IP Creator, 30% for the University, and 10% for InnovateUC fund. g.
In the case of promising research projects assessed by the KMID and its Innovation Technology Committee, the University has the option to seek patent or copyright protection. h.
On licensing agreement (PNC:PRE-FO-55). i.
The licensing agreement must clearly state the intellectual property being licensed, the scope of the license, and the rights and obligations of both parties. ii.
The licensing agreement must include a provision for payment of royalties. iii.
The licensing agreement must include provisions for confidentiality and non-disclosure of the intellectual property. iv.
The licensing agreement must include provisions for termination and enforcement of the agreement. v.
The licensing agreement must comply with the provisions outlined in RA 8293 Sections 87 and 88. vi.
Royalty sharing shall be 60% for the IP Creator, 30% for the University, and 10% for InnovateUC fund.
6.
IP Portfolio Management a.
The KMID is responsible for maintaining records of intellectual property at the University of Cabuyao.
It will oversee deadlines for payment obligations associated with the maintenance or annuity fees of protected intellectual property.
Within a reasonable timeframe, the KMID will facilitate the submission of a letter request for such payments.

b.
The KMID will uphold income and expense accounting records for each intellectual property, enabling the Accounting Department to calculate revenue-sharing allocations accurately.
7.
Enforcement of Intellectual Property Rights a.
The University shall take appropriate legal action to enforce its intellectual property rights against any infringement, misappropriation, or unauthorized use. b.
The University shall seek damages and other remedies available under applicable laws, regulations, and contractual obligations. c.
The University shall cooperate with law enforcement agencies and other stakeholders in the enforcement of intellectual property rights. d.
The University recognizes the exclusive rights of inventors, authors and artists over their intellectual property creations.
For this reason, it shall protect the rights of the owners of intellectual property over all forms of infringement such as: i.
Photocopying of printed materials or copying of computer software without the permission of the author/s or creator/s, subject to the rules on fair use of copyrighted work and the other exceptions thereto as stated in the Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines (RA 8293); ii.
Use, distribution, transfer, rental, sale, or production of counterfeit, unlicensed or pirated intellectual property contained in optical media as defined under the Optical Media Act of 2003 (RA 9239); iii.
Violation of the confidentiality rule iv.
Unauthorized use, distribution, transfer, rental, sale or production of university-owned intellectual property; v.
Plagiarism and other forms of academic dishonesty vi.
All other acts analogous to the foregoing e.
